appellations.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Fournières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Fournières is a 5.6 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru below Corton Perrières, on the southern side of the hill. Tollot-Beaut makes a fine, fruity version.

It lies on the gentle slope below Corton Les Perrières, between Les Chaillots and the Clos du Chapitre. Tollot-Beaut's Fournières, from a family estate in Chorey-lès-Beaune, is the most widely seen and shows the ripe, red-fruited, approachable side of Aloxe.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The slope is gentle, about 6% on average, and the soil is deeper here than on the grand cru above, which is the main reason the wine is rounder and readier.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits about 30 m below Corton Les Perrières, a measure of how quickly the grand cru gives way to premier cru on the gentler lower slope.

appellations.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Valozières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Valozières is a 6.6 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru just below Corton Bressandes, on the south side of the hill. Its red is firm and spicy, close to a light Corton.

Les Chaillots and Les Paulands lie alongside, and its wines are a good-value glimpse of red Corton: spicy, firm and dark-fruited, ready a few years earlier than the grand cru.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, iron-rich brown limestone-clay. The gradient flattens to about 8% here, and the iron-stained brown soil is deeper than on the Bressandes slope just above, giving fleshier, earlier wines.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits directly below Corton Les Bressandes, at the point where the slope flattens out.

appellations.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Vercots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Vercots is a 4.3 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru at the southern edge of the commune, toward Savigny. Follin-Arbelet and Antonin Guyon make it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.

Its neighbour Les Guérets and Savigny's Les Lavières share the same flatter ground, and its wines are softer and more red-fruited than the premiers crus under the grand cru. Follin-Arbelet's version is a reliable reference.
appellations.terroir: Almost flat, south exposure at about 245 m, on brown limestone-clay. Being away from the hill of Corton, it lacks the marl and iron of the grand cru slopes, which is why its wines are lighter and more fruit-led.
appellations.nerd_note: Its neighbour Les Guérets is the other premier cru on the Savigny side of Aloxe.

appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Ursules is a walled 1.3 ha monopole of Maison Louis Jadot within Les Vignes Franches, at the southern end of Beaune. It belonged to the Ursuline nuns before the Revolution, and the Jadot family bought it in 1826, decades before the négociant house was founded in 1859. The wine is firm, dark-fruited and long-lived.

The clos sits on the southern part of Beaune's slope, within Les Vignes Franches, with Les Aigrots above and Les Pertuisots alongside, on iron-rich brown soil. Jadot's red is darker and firmer than most Beaunes, with a Pommard-like structure from the southern end of the appellation, and it ages for 15 years or more.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 270 m, moderately steep. Brown limestone-clay with iron.
appellations.nerd_note: It was the Jadot family's first vineyard, and the house still treats it as its flagship Beaune.

appellations.summary:
The Clos du Roi is a 13.3 ha premier cru at the northern end of Beaune, below Les Marconnets. Like its namesake in Corton, it is thought to have passed from the Dukes of Burgundy to the French crown. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.

En Genêt, Blanches Fleurs and Les Cents Vignes lie alongside, and its wines are firm and dark-fruited; Tollot-Beaut's and Chanson's versions show the more structured side of northern Beaune.
appellations.terroir: Gentle south slope at 230 to 245 m, brown limestone-clay. The gradient is very gentle, about 2%, and the deeper soil at the foot of the Marconnets slope gives the wine its fleshy core.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the few Beaune premier crus facing almost due south.

appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Dames Hospitalières and Hugues et Louis Bétault both include La Mignotte.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Le Bas des Teurons
match: Beaune premier cru Le Bas des Teurons
Beaune 1er Cru Le Bas des Teurons
Beaune Premier Cru Le Bas des Teurons
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Le Bas des Teurons is a 6.7 ha premier cru below Les Teurons, on the lower slope. The wine is supple and fruity.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, deep brown clay. On the map it lies below Les Grèves and Les Teurons.
appellations.nerd_note: *Bas* means lower: the same climat continues upslope as Les Teurons.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Le Clos des Mouches
match: Beaune premier cru Le Clos des Mouches
Beaune 1er Cru Le Clos des Mouches
Beaune Premier Cru Le Clos des Mouches
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Le Clos des Mouches is Beaune's most famous premier cru and one of the few Côte de Beaune climats equally celebrated for red and white. It lies at the southern end of the appellation, against the Pommard boundary, and at 25.3 ha it is one of the larger premier crus of the Côte. The *mouches* are usually said to be honeybees (*mouches à miel*), once kept in hives on the slope.

Maison Joseph Drouhin built its reputation here: Maurice Drouhin began buying parcels in 1921, and the house now owns more than half the climat, about 14 ha. Its white Clos des Mouches, from the upper slope, is rich and nutty with a mineral finish, a Beaune white that can rival Meursault; its red is perfumed, round and silky. Chanson also makes both colours.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 250 to 310 m, moderately steep. White marl and limestone on the upper slope, where most Chardonnay is planted; brown, iron-tinged limestone-clay lower down for Pinot Noir.
appellations.nerd_note: The upper, marly slope is planted mostly to Chardonnay and the lower slope to Pinot Noir, so one climat name covers what are really two different vineyards.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Aigrots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Aigrots is a large 18.7 ha premier cru on the upper southern slope of Beaune, above Les Vignes Franches. Michel Lafarge makes both red and white. The wine is fresh and fine.

It sits high on the southern part of Beaune's slope, above Les Vignes Franches and the Clos des Ursules and beside the Clos des Mouches, on stony limestone with marl. It is one of the few Beaune premier crus where white is as important as red, and Lafarge's white Clos des Aigrots is a good example.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 310 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils with marl. The upper slope here climbs above 300 m, and the white marl that appears there is the reason Chardonnay does so well.
appellations.nerd_note: The upper slope's marl suits Chardonnay, which is why Les Aigrots makes good white.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Avaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Avaux is a large 11.1 ha premier cru on the lower central slope of Beaune. The wine is supple and fruity.
appellations.terroir: Gentle east-southeast slope at 230 to 250 m, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Sizies, above Belissand and beside Clos des Avaux and Les Tuvilains.
appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Maurice Drouhin includes Les Avaux.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Boucherottes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Boucherottes is a 8.6 ha premier cru at the southern end of Beaune, against the Pommard boundary. The wine is firm and dark-fruited, close to Pommard in style.

It runs into Pommard's Les Boucherottes and Les Petits Epenots, below the Clos des Mouches and beside Les Epenotes. Its wines have something of Pommard's depth in a more perfumed Beaune frame, and Jadot's version is a reliable reference.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, iron-rich brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The same climat name continues into Pommard.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Bressandes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Bressandes is a large 17.2 ha premier cru on the upper slope at the northern end of Beaune, above Les Cents Vignes and Les Toussaints. The wine is firm, perfumed and structured, one of Beaune's longest-lived reds.

It sits high on the northern part of Beaune's slope, above Les Toussaints, Les Cents Vignes and Les Fèves and below the woods, on thin, stony soil. That steep, stony position gives one of Beaune's firmest and longest-lived reds; Albert Morot's version, from a family estate in Beaune's old Château de la Creusotte, is a classic.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 240 to 310 m, slope around 20%. Stony limestone soils, thin on the upper slope.
appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Guigone de Salins and Dames Hospitalières both include Bressandes.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Cents Vignes
match: Beaune premier cru Les Cents Vignes
Beaune Premier Cru Les Cents Vignes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Cents Vignes ('hundred vines') is a large 23.5 ha premier cru on the lower slope at the northern end of Beaune. The wine is supple, fruity and early-drinking.

Les Bressandes and Les Fèves lie above it, Les Toussaints and the Clos du Roi alongside. Its deeper soil gives ripe, round wines that drink early; the Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Nicolas Rolin and Rousseau-Deslandes both draw on it.
appellations.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at 225 to 240 m, deep brown limestone-clay. At about 225 to 240 m on an almost flat gradient, it is one of the lowest of Beaune's northern premier crus, and its deep soil retains water well in dry summers.
appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Nicolas Rolin includes Cents Vignes.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Chouacheux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Chouacheux is a 5.0 ha premier cru on the lower southern slope of Beaune. Jadot makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Vignes Franches and Les Boucherottes and beside Les Tuvilains and Clos Saint-Landry.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the lesser-known Beaune premier crus in Jadot's range.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Epenotes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Epenotes is a 8.0 ha premier cru at the southern end of Beaune, on the boundary with Pommard's Epenots. The wine is supple and perfumed, a Beaune with some of Pommard's depth.

It runs straight into Pommard's Les Petits Epenots and Les Boucherottes. The Beaune side of the Epenots makes a slightly softer, more perfumed wine than the Pommard side, but the two share the same deep, gravelly brown soil.
appellations.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at 235 to 245 m, brown limestone-clay. The flat ground, around 3% gradient, and deep soil give a soft, generous structure; the climat is one of the easiest places to taste the transition from Beaune to Pommard.
appellations.nerd_note: Spelled Epenotes in Beaune and Epenots in Pommard, it is one climat split by the commune line.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Fèves
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Fèves is a 4.8 ha premier cru on the northern part of Beaune's slope, below Les Bressandes. Chanson's Clos des Fèves monopole fills most of it. The wine is fine and perfumed.

Les Bressandes and A l'Ecu lie above it and Les Cents Vignes below. Chanson's Clos des Fèves, which occupies most of it, is one of Beaune's most refined reds: perfumed, red-fruited and silky.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Chanson's Clos des Fèves is its flagship Beaune premier cru.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Grèves
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Grèves is the heart of Beaune and its largest premier cru, about 31 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 31.3 ha), on the middle of the slope above the town. *Grèves* means gravel, and the soil is gravelly and well-drained, which gives some of the most complete reds of Beaune: perfumed, ripe and spicy, with a firm, fine tannin.

Its best-known parcel is Bouchard Père et Fils' 'Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus', a 3.9 ha monopole within the climat whose name recalls the 17th-century Carmelite nun Marguerite du Saint-Sacrement, who is said to have predicted the birth of Louis XIV. Jadot makes a white Beaune Grèves 'Le Clos Blanc'.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 300 m, moderately steep. Gravelly limestone soils over Bathonian limestone, with iron-stained clay in the lower part.
appellations.nerd_note: The Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus was owned by the Carmelites until the Revolution; Bouchard bought it in 1791.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Marconnets
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Marconnets is a 9.4 ha premier cru at the northern end of Beaune, against the Savigny boundary. The wine is firm and dark-fruited, one of the more structured Beaunes.

The Clos du Roi and En Genêt lie below it and En l'Orme beside it. Its iron-rich soils give one of Beaune's most structured reds, darker and firmer than the central premiers crus, and Bouchard's and Chanson's versions need several years to open.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 290 m, moderately steep. Iron-rich brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The same climat name continues into Savigny-lès-Beaune.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Montrevenots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Montrevenots is a 8.5 ha premier cru high on the slope above the Clos des Mouches, at the southern end of Beaune. Jean-Marc Boillot makes it. The wine is fresh and fine, red or white.
appellations.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 295 to 335 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: At over 300 m it is the highest premier cru in Beaune.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Perrières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Perrières is a 3.2 ha premier cru on the northern part of Beaune's slope, on stony ground once quarried. The wine is firm and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 245 to 295 m, slope around 22%, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Perrières is one of the commonest climat names on the Côte d'Or, always marking a former quarry.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Reversés
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Reversés is a 4.8 ha premier cru on the lower central slope of Beaune. The wine is soft and fruity.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Clos de la Mousse and Les Teurons and beside Les Sceaux and Belissand.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus in Beaune.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Sceaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Sceaux is a 3.1 ha premier cru at the foot of Beaune's central slope, next to the town. The wine is soft and fruity.
appellations.terroir: Flat, east-southeast exposure at about 225 m, deep brown clay.
appellations.nerd_note: At around 225 m it is one of the lowest premier crus in Beaune, almost at the edge of the town.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Seurey
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Seurey is a small 1.2 ha premier cru on the lower central slope of Beaune. The wine is supple and fruity.
appellations.terroir: Southwest-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Champs Pimont and beside Les Avaux, Clos de la Mousse and Clos des Avaux.
appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Guigone de Salins includes Les Seurey.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Sizies
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Sizies is a 8.6 ha premier cru on the lower southern slope of Beaune. The wine is supple and fruity.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Aigrots, above Les Avaux and Les Tuvilains and beside Pertuisots.
appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Hugues et Louis Bétault includes Les Sizies.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Teurons
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Teurons is a large 21.5 ha premier cru in the centre of Beaune, below Aux Cras and next to Les Grèves. The wine is perfumed, ripe and round, with red fruit and a silky tannin, one of Beaune's most charming premier crus.

It sits in the centre of Beaune's slope, with Aux Cras and Champs Pimont above, Les Grèves to the north and Le Bas des Teurons below. Its gravelly soil gives ripe, perfumed wines with fine tannin, and it is often ranked just behind Les Grèves among Beaune's central premier crus.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 225 to 265 m, gentle slope. Gravelly brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Les Teurons and Le Bas des Teurons together make up the second-largest premier cru area in Beaune after Les Grèves.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Toussaints
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Toussaints is a 6.4 ha premier cru on the lower slope between Les Grèves and Les Cents Vignes. Albert Morot makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Grèves and Les Bressandes and beside Les Cents Vignes.
appellations.nerd_note: The name means All Saints.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Tuvilains
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Tuvilains is a 8.9 ha premier cru on the lower southern slope of Beaune. The wine is soft and fruity.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Sizies and Clos Saint-Landry, above Belissand and beside Les Avaux.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits on the flat ground at the foot of the southern slope, between the Clos Saint-Landry and Les Chouacheux.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Les Vignes Franches
match: Beaune premier cru Les Vignes Franches
Beaune Premier Cru Les Vignes Franches
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Vignes Franches is a 8.5 ha premier cru on the southern slope of Beaune, toward Pommard. Jadot's Clos des Ursules is inside it. The wine is firm and dark-fruited, with Pommard's structure.

It sits at the southern end of Beaune, with Les Aigrots and the Clos des Mouches above and Les Boucherottes and Les Chouacheux alongside, on iron-rich brown soil. Its wines are firm and dark, with a Pommard-like structure, and Jadot's Clos des Ursules inside it is the most famous wine of the climat.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 270 m, moderately steep, iron-rich brown limestone-clay. Iron oxides give the soil a reddish tinge similar to Pommard's Rugiens, and the gradient steepens toward the Clos des Mouches above.
appellations.nerd_note: *Franches* is usually explained as 'free': vines once exempt from feudal dues.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Montée Rouge
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Montée Rouge is a 4.7 ha premier cru high on the central slope of Beaune, named for its red, iron-stained soil. The wine is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 245 to 300 m, iron-rich red soils. On the map it lies below Aux Coucherias, above La Mignotte and beside Champs Pimont.
appellations.nerd_note: *Montée* means rise: the slope here climbs sharply toward the woods.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Pertuisots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Pertuisots is a 5.3 ha premier cru on the southern slope of Beaune, near Les Vignes Franches. Domaine des Croix makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Aigrots and Clos des Ursules, above Clos Saint-Landry and beside Les Sizies.
appellations.nerd_note: A *pertuis* is a narrow passage, perhaps an old path through the vines.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Sur les Grèves
match: Beaune premier cru Sur les Grèves
Beaune Premier Cru Sur les Grèves
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Sur les Grèves ('above the Grèves') is a steep 3.8 ha premier cru above Les Grèves. The wine is firm and fresh, with red fruit and a stony finish.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 260 to 310 m, slope around 25%. Thin, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Its walled northern section, the Clos Sainte-Anne, has a premier cru name of its own.

appellations.name: Beaune premier cru Sur les Grèves - Clos Saint-Anne
match: Beaune premier cru Sur les Grèves - Clos Saint-Anne
Beaune 1er Cru Sur les Grèves - Clos Saint-Anne
Beaune Premier Cru Sur les Grèves - Clos Saint-Anne
Beaune premier cru Sur les Grèves Clos Sainte-Anne
Beaune 1er Cru Sur les Grèves Clos Sainte-Anne

appellations.summary: The Clos Sainte-Anne is a 0.77 ha walled section of Sur les Grèves, above Beaune's Les Grèves. Maison Jaffelin makes it as a monopole. The wine is firm and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 275 to 310 m, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Sur les Grèves and Les Grèves.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest named premier crus in Beaune.

appellations.name: Blagny premier cru Hameau de Blagny

Blagny Premier Cru Hameau de Blagny
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Hameau de Blagny ('the hamlet of Blagny') is a 4.2 ha premier cru around the hamlet, on the Puligny side. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru; white is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 315 to 340 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: The hamlet has only a handful of houses and a chapel.

appellations.name: Blagny premier cru La Garenne
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: The red side of La Garenne: 9.9 ha high above Puligny, near the hamlet of Blagny. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru; white is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 375 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Puligny-Montrachet's Sous le Puits and above Puligny-Montrachet's Champ Gain, Puligny-Montrachet's Hameau de Blagny and Saint-Aubin's Les Murgers des dents de chien.
appellations.nerd_note: *Garenne* means a rabbit warren.

appellations.name: Blagny premier cru La Jeunellotte
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: The red side of La Jeunellotte: 5.0 ha high above Meursault, in the hamlet of Blagny. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 325 to 355 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Puligny-Montrachet's Sous le Puits and Meursault's Les Ravelles and above Meursault's Blagny and Meursault's La Pièce sous le Bois.
appellations.nerd_note: White from the same vines is Meursault premier cru.

Blagny 1er Cru La Pièce sous le Bois
Blagny Premier Cru La Pièce sous le Bois

appellations.summary: The red side of La Pièce sous le Bois: 11.3 ha high above Meursault, in the hamlet of Blagny. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru, a firm, red-fruited Pinot Noir.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 310 to 345 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Blagny AOC is red-only, while white from the same slopes takes the name of Meursault or Puligny-Montrachet.

appellations.name: Blagny premier cru Sous Blagny
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: The red side of Sous Blagny: 2.2 ha just below the hamlet. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 300 to 335 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Meursault's Blagny and La Jeunellotte and above Meursault's Sous le Dos d'Ane and Puligny-Montrachet's Les Chalumaux.
appellations.nerd_note: White from the same vines is Meursault premier cru.

appellations.name: Blagny premier cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
match: Blagny premier cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
Blagny 1er Cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
Blagny Premier Cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: The red side of Sous le Dos d'Ane: 5.2 ha below the hamlet of Blagny. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 320 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Meursault's Blagny, Meursault's La Pièce sous le Bois and Sous Blagny and above Meursault's Perrières.
appellations.nerd_note: White from the same vines is Meursault premier cru.

appellations.name: Blagny premier cru Sous le Puits
match: Blagny premier cru Sous le Puits
Blagny Premier Cru Sous le Puits
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: The red side of Sous le Puits: 6.8 ha high above Puligny, at the top of the Blagny slope. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru; white is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 400 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: At around 400 m at its top it is one of the highest premier crus in the Côte d'Or.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Berdiot
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Berdiot is a small 3.6 ha premier cru on the right bank, near Fyé, standing on its own rather than as part of a larger group. Its wines are fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 175 to 210 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premiers crus of Chablis.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Beugnons
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Beugnons is a 14.5 ha satellite of Vaillons on the left bank southwest of Chablis, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its wines are fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 200 to 265 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies above Chatains and Roncières.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the higher sites of the Vaillons group.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Chatains
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Châtains is a 7.3 ha satellite of Vaillons on the left bank southwest of Chablis, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its wines are fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 205 to 250 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies below Beugnons and above Roncières and Vaillons.
appellations.nerd_note: The name refers to chestnut trees (*châtaigniers*).

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Chaume de Talvat

Chablis Premier Cru Chaume de Talvat

appellations.nerd_note: At just over a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus in Chablis.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Bréchain
