Chablis Premier Cru Côte de Bréchain
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Côte de Bréchain is a 11.1 ha satellite of Montée de Tonnerre on the right bank of the Serein, at the northern end of that group, and its wine may be sold under the Montée de Tonnerre name. It shares the group's saline, mineral style.
appellations.terroir: West-northwest-facing at 170 to 225 m, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: The Bréchain valley here separates the Montée de Tonnerre group from the grand cru Blanchot, so the premier cru sits directly across a small combe from the grands crus.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Jouan
match: Chablis premier cru Côte de Jouan
Chablis Premier Cru Côte de Jouan
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Côte de Jouan is a 12.6 ha Chablis premier cru in Courgis, west of the town on the left bank of the Serein. The wine is fresh, crisp and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 215 to 290 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Courgis, high on the left bank, has three premier crus: Côte de Jouan, Les Beauregards and Chaume de Talvat.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Léchet
match: Chablis premier cru Côte de Léchet
Chablis Premier Cru Côte de Léchet
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Côte de Léchet is a large 53.9 ha premier cru on the left bank above the hamlet of Milly, west of Chablis. Its steep, east-southeast-facing slope gives a tense, mineral Chablis with a stony finish.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 150 to 225 m, slope around 20%, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Milly, like Fyé and Poinchy, is a hamlet of the commune of Chablis.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Savant
match: Chablis premier cru Côte de Savant
Chablis Premier Cru Côte de Savant
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Côte de Savant is a small 1.4 ha satellite of Beauroy in Beine, on the left bank west of Chablis, sold as Beauroy or under its own name.
appellations.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 180 to 220 m, slope around 29%, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: With Troesmes it is one of the two satellites of Beauroy.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Forêts
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Forêts (also La Forest) is a 22.5 ha satellite of Montmains on the left bank southwest of Chablis, sold as Montmains or under its own name. Vincent Dauvissat's La Forest and Raveneau's Forêts made it famous: taut, deep and long-lived, among the finest left-bank wines.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 180 to 225 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: With Butteaux it is one of two Montmains satellites that leading growers prefer to bottle under their own names.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Fourchaume
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Fourchaume is the largest and one of the most celebrated Chablis premier crus, a long band of slopes on the right bank of the Serein running north from the grands crus. The INAO delimitation of the main name covers 99.4 ha across Maligny, La Chapelle-Vaupelteigne and Fontenay-près-Chablis, and satellite climats such as Vaupulent, Côte de Fontenay, Vaulorent and L'Homme Mort may also be sold as Fourchaume. Its southern end, Vaulorent, touches the grand cru Les Preuses and is often ranked among the very best premier crus of Chablis.

Fourchaume is the richest, roundest of the premier crus: ripe citrus, white peach and a creamy texture over the classic Chablis spine of oyster-shell minerality. It is approachable earlier than Montée de Tonnerre or Mont de Milieu.
appellations.terroir: Southwest-facing slopes at 130 to 195 m, catching afternoon sun. Kimmeridgian marl and limestone full of tiny fossil oysters (*Exogyra virgula*), the same formation as the grands crus.
appellations.nerd_note: Fourchaume faces west and southwest, so its grapes ripen in warm afternoon light, one reason its wines are fuller than the southeast-facing premier crus of Fleys.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru L'Homme Mort
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: L'Homme Mort ('the dead man') is a 25.3 ha satellite of Fourchaume in Maligny, at the northern end of the Fourchaume slopes, sold as Fourchaume or under its own name. Its wines are ripe and round.
appellations.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 130 to 175 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: The macabre name is old, and no one is sure of its origin.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Les Beauregards
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Beauregards is a 21.3 ha Chablis premier cru in Courgis, on the left bank west of the town. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 230 to 300 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: *Beauregard* means 'fine view'.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Les Fourneaux
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Fourneaux is a 35.8 ha Chablis premier cru in Fleys, east of Mont de Milieu, on the right bank of the Serein. Its satellites include Morein and Côte des Prés Girots. The wine is fresh, mineral and fruity.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 180 to 240 m, steep in places, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: *Fourneaux* refers to old kilns; Savigny and Mercurey have premier crus with the same name.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Les Lys
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Lys is a 14.5 ha satellite of Vaillons on the left bank of the Serein, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its north-northeast tilt makes it one of the cooler premier cru sites, and its wines are lean, floral and racy.
appellations.terroir: North-northeast-facing at 190 to 235 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Its cooler exposure, unusual for a premier cru, gives some of the most austere Chablis in youth.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Les Épinottes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Epinottes is a 26.9 ha satellite of Vaillons on the lower left-bank slopes near the town of Chablis, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its wines are fresh and supple.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 155 to 190 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier cru sites of the left bank.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Mont de Milieu
match: Chablis premier cru Mont de Milieu
Chablis Premier Cru Mont de Milieu
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Mont de Milieu is one of the classic right-bank Chablis premier crus, an 18.2 ha slope in Fleys, east of Montée de Tonnerre. Its name, 'the middle hill', is usually explained by its old position on the frontier between the Duchy of Burgundy and the County of Champagne. Its wines are among the most structured and long-lived of Chablis: tight, saline and mineral in youth, opening after five to ten years into citrus, hazelnut and iodine.

Les Fourneaux lies further east on the same right-bank slopes. Billaud-Simon's and Pinson's versions are references.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 175 to 235 m, moderately steep. Kimmeridgian marl and limestone with fossil oysters; the southeast exposure gives ripeness while keeping acidity.
producers: Domaine Alice et Olivier De Moor
appellations.nerd_note: Mont de Milieu and Montée de Tonnerre are the two right-bank premier crus most often compared with the grands crus.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Montée de Tonnerre
match: Chablis premier cru Montée de Tonnerre
Chablis Premier Cru Montée de Tonnerre
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Montée de Tonnerre is usually ranked the finest premier cru of Chablis, the one most often described as a grand cru in all but name. It lies on the right bank of the Serein just east of the grand cru slope, separated from Blanchot by a small side valley, on the old road toward Tonnerre that gives it its name. This polygon is the lieu-dit itself, 5.5 ha; the principal name also covers Chapelot, Pied d'Aloup and Côte de Bréchain, which may all be sold as Montée de Tonnerre.

Its wines combine the grands crus' density with a cool, saline cut: citrus, white flowers and oyster shell in youth, then hazelnut and iodine after eight to ten years. Raveneau's Montée de Tonnerre and Chapelot are among the most sought-after white wines in France.
appellations.terroir: West-facing at 160 to 200 m, with the warm afternoon exposure of the right bank. Kimmeridgian marl and limestone full of small fossil oysters (*Exogyra virgula*), the same formation as the grands crus next door.
appellations.nerd_note: Raveneau bottles Chapelot separately from its Montée de Tonnerre, which is one of the few chances to taste a Chablis satellite climat on its own.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Morein
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Morein is a 10.4 ha satellite of Les Fourneaux in Fleys, on the right bank east of Chablis, sold as Les Fourneaux or under its own name.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 180 to 235 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies below Les Fourneaux.
appellations.nerd_note: With Côte des Prés Girots it makes up the Fourneaux group.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Roncières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Roncières is a 22.4 ha climat of the Vaillons group on the left bank southwest of Chablis, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its wines are supple and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 175 to 205 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies below Vaillons, Chatains and Beugnons and above Les Épinottes.
appellations.nerd_note: *Ronces* are brambles; Nuits-Saint-Georges has a premier cru called Roncière.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Sécher
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Sécher (also spelt Séchet) is a 12.2 ha satellite of Vaillons on the left bank southwest of Chablis, and its wine may be sold as Vaillons. Vincent Dauvissat's Séchet is the reference: taut, citrus-scented and long.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 185 to 210 m, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: The geodata used for this map lists Sécher under Roncières; the BIVB listing places both Sécher and Roncières in the Vaillons group.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Vaillons
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Vaillons is the best-known premier cru of the left bank of the Serein, on the slopes southwest of the town of Chablis. This polygon is the lieu-dit Les Vaillons, 7.5 ha; the principal name also covers Châtains, Sécher, Beugnons, Les Lys, Mélinots, Roncières and Les Epinottes, so a bottle labelled Vaillons can come from a wide spread of slopes.

Left-bank Chablis faces southeast and gets the morning sun, and Vaillons is the archetype: lean, citrus-driven and mineral when young, with less weight than the right-bank premiers crus but great precision and a long, chalky finish. It is one of the most widely produced premiers crus and a good test of a grower.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 185 to 225 m, on Kimmeridgian marl and limestone; the soils are a little stonier and lighter than on the right bank.
producers: Domaine Christian Moreau Père et Fils
appellations.nerd_note: The Vaillons group is one of the largest in Chablis; growers increasingly label its satellites, such as Séchet or Beugnons, separately to show the differences between them.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Vau Ligneau
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Vau Ligneau is a 10.3 ha premier cru in Beine, on the left bank west of Chablis, standing on its own. Its wines are fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 185 to 225 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: *Vau* means a small valley, a common word in Chablis climat names.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Vau de Vey
match: Chablis premier cru Vau de Vey
Chablis Premier Cru Vau de Vey
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Vau de Vey is a 13.2 ha premier cru in Beine, on the left bank west of Chablis, with Vaux Ragons as its satellite. Its steep slope gives a fresh, mineral Chablis.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 155 to 230 m, slope around 27%, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the steepest premier cru slopes of Chablis.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Vaucoupin
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Vaucoupin is a 47.4 ha Chablis premier cru in Chichée, southeast of the town, on the right bank of the Serein. The wine is fresh and mineral, with good ripeness from its south-southwest exposure.
appellations.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 165 to 265 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Grossot's Vaucoupin is one of the reference versions of this lesser-known right-bank site.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Vaugiraut
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Vaugiraut is a 7.0 ha satellite of Vosgros in Chichée, southeast of Chablis. Its wine may be sold as Vosgros.
appellations.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 185 to 205 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies below Vosgros.
appellations.nerd_note: It may carry its own name or Vosgros'.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Vaupulent
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Vaupulent is a 2.6 ha satellite of Fourchaume in La Chapelle-Vaupelteigne, on the right bank north of the grands crus. Its wine is usually sold as Fourchaume. The style is the same: ripe, round Chablis with a mineral core.
appellations.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 155 to 205 m, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Like Vaulorent and L'Homme Mort, it may carry either its own name or Fourchaume's.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Vosgros
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Vosgros is a 22.6 ha Chablis premier cru in Chichée, southeast of the town, with its satellite Vaugiraut. The wine is fresh, mineral and citrus-driven.
appellations.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 185 to 215 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies above Vaugiraut.
producers: Domaine Gilbert Picq et ses Fils
appellations.nerd_note: Its west-southwest exposure gives afternoon sun, like Fourchaume's.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Aux Beaux Bruns
match: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Aux Beaux Bruns
Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Aux Beaux Bruns
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Aux Beaux Bruns is a 1.5 ha premier cru below the village, near the Route des Grands Crus. The name means 'fine browns', probably for its soil colour. Barthod's Beaux Bruns is the best-known; the wine is deeper and more structured than most lower-slope Chambolle.
appellations.terroir: Flat, southeast exposure at about 265 m, on deep brown clay over limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Barthod's Beaux Bruns is often the most solidly built of her premier crus, a sign of its deeper soil.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Aux Combottes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.83 ha on the lower slope near the Route des Grands Crus, not to be confused with Les Combottes nearby or with Gevrey's Aux Combottes. The wine is a supple Chambolle premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 260 m, almost flat, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Chambolle has two premier crus called Combottes, a reminder that Burgundy's climats were named by farmers, not marketers.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Aux Echanges
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A small premier cru of 0.93 ha on the lower slope near the Route des Grands Crus. The name records a land exchange. The wine is a soft, red-fruited Chambolle premier cru.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 260 m, nearly flat, on brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Aux Combottes, Aux Beaux Bruns and Les Groseilles.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus in Chambolle.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Derrière la Grange
match: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Derrière la Grange
Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Derrière la Grange
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.47 ha just north of the village, behind an old barn (*grange*). Amiot-Servelle's version is the best-known. The wine is perfumed and fine-boned.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 275 m, on thin limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: With Les Lavrottes and Les Fuées it forms the group of small premier crus just north of the village houses.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru La Combe d'Orveau
match: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru La Combe d'Orveau
Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru La Combe d'Orveau
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
La Combe d'Orveau lies at the southern end of Chambolle, beside Musigny, on the side of the small combe that separates Chambolle from Vosne's En Orveaux. The INAO delimitation gives 2.2 ha of premier cru; much of the lieu-dit is village Chambolle. The wine is cool, perfumed and fine, close to Musigny's elegance in the best parcels.

The combe is a small, cool side valley, and the premier cru vines sit on its north-facing flank next to Musigny, on thin, stony soil. In ripe vintages that coolness gives wines of exceptional poise and perfume; Bruno Clavelier's old-vine bottling and Perrot-Minot's are often compared to a junior Musigny.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 295 m, moderately steep. Thin, stony limestone soils, cooled by air from the combe.
appellations.nerd_note: Musigny itself includes a slice of the Combe d'Orveau lieu-dit, so a few growers own Combe d'Orveau vines that are grand cru.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Amoureuses
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Amoureuses is the most famous premier cru in Burgundy and, on price, often beats grands crus such as Clos de Vougeot and Echezeaux. It lies directly below Musigny, separated from it only by a narrow track, and runs down to the walls of Clos de Vougeot. The INAO delimitation measures 5.3 ha; the planted area is usually given as 5.4 ha.

The wine is the purest expression of Chambolle: pale to mid ruby, intensely perfumed (rose, violet, raspberry, wild strawberry), silky and weightless in the mouth but very long, with a fine, almost invisible tannin. Where Musigny adds depth and gravity, Amoureuses gives grace and lift.

The largest holder is Domaine Robert Groffier (about 1.1 ha); others include de Vogüé, Mugnier, Roumier, Drouhin and Amiot-Servelle, and for each it is one of the most sought-after wines in the cellar.
appellations.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 240 to 280 m. Thin, pebbly soil over hard Comblanchien and Bathonian limestone, with very little clay at the surface and fissured rock close below. The vineyard falls away in a slight bowl toward Clos de Vougeot, so drainage is excellent.
producers: Domaine Robert Groffier Père et Fils
appellations.nerd_note: Groffier's 1.1 ha make it the Amoureuses most often seen; the half-hectare holdings of Mugnier and de Vogüé and Roumier's even smaller parcel yield only a few barrels a year.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Baudes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Baudes sits just below Bonnes-Mares, at 3.5 ha. Its wines have the structure of their grand cru neighbour: firm, darker-fruited Chambolle, often slow to open.

Les Baudes lies just below the southern tip of Bonnes-Mares, between Les Sentiers and Les Noirots, and its wines carry something of the grand cru's structure and dark fruit. Barthod's Baudes is among the firmest of her nine-odd Chambolle premier crus and usually needs several years to open.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at about 270 m, on brown limestone-clay over Comblanchien limestone. The soil here contains more clay than in the southern premier crus of Chambolle, the same feature that gives Bonnes-Mares its power.
appellations.nerd_note: Les Baudes, Les Sentiers and Les Fuées are the premier crus that touch Bonnes-Mares, and all three share some of its firmness.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Borniques
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Les Borniques is a 1.4 ha premier cru touching Musigny on its northern side, above Les Amoureuses. The wine shares some of Musigny's depth and perfume and is one of the less-known gems of the village.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 275 to 285 m, on thin, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of three premier crus that touch Musigny, with Les Amoureuses and La Combe d'Orveau.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Carrières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.52 ha near Les Chatelots, named for an old quarry. The wine is a perfumed Chambolle premier cru, rarely bottled alone.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at about 265 m on stony limestone. On the map it lies beside Les Chatelots and Les Gruenchers.
appellations.nerd_note: Quarries were dug all along the Côte for building stone and for the lime kilns that made mortar.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Chabiots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A 1.5 ha premier cru above Les Amoureuses and near Les Borniques, south of the village. It gives a perfumed, fine-boned Chambolle with good tension.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 270 to 280 m on stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Borniques and above Les Amoureuses, Les Plantes and Les Hauts Doix.
appellations.nerd_note: Its neighbour Les Amoureuses lies just downslope.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Charmes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Charmes is one of Chambolle's largest premier crus, at 9.3 ha, on the gentle lower slope east of the village between Les Amoureuses and the Route des Grands Crus. The name refers to *chaume*, fallow land, rather than charm, though the wine has plenty: soft, round, cherry-fruited Chambolle that drinks well young.

It lacks the tension of Les Amoureuses or Les Cras, but good growers make a deeply perfumed wine with Chambolle's velvet texture.

Les Charmes is also a good illustration of how Chambolle's premier crus change with altitude: the lower, flatter end near the Route des Grands Crus gives softer, fruit-forward wines, while the upper end toward Les Chabiots and Les Feusselottes, on thinner soil, gives more perfume and tension. Labels rarely say which end, so the producer matters.
appellations.terroir: Almost flat, east exposure at 250 to 270 m. Deeper brown limestone-clay than the upper premier crus, over Comblanchien limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Barthod's Charmes is a good place to start a tasting of the domaine's nine-odd Chambolle premier crus.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Chatelots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Les Chatelots is a 3.0 ha premier cru just east of the village, on the gentle slope toward Les Charmes. It gives a perfumed, medium-bodied Chambolle with red fruit and fine tannin.
appellations.terroir: Gentle east-northeast slope at about 265 m, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Barthod bottles it separately, which lets you compare it with her Charmes and Beaux Bruns just downslope.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Combottes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A 0.72 ha premier cru on the gentle slope between Les Charmes and the village. Roumier's Combottes is the best-known. The wine is perfumed, red-fruited and silky.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 265 m, on brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Charmes, Les Chatelots, Les Plantes and Aux Combottes.
appellations.nerd_note: Roumier makes only a few barrels of it each year, and it is one of the domaine's least-known wines.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Cras
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Cras lies above the village, on the slope toward the Combe d'Ambin, at 3.4 ha. *Cras* means stony ground, and the soil here is thin and pebbly. The wine is Chambolle's most mineral and structured premier cru after Les Amoureuses: red cherry, violet and crushed stone, with a firm, fine tannin that needs time. Roumier and Barthod make the reference wines.

It sits on the upper slope northwest of the village, above Derrière la Grange and beside Les Fuées, in the cool air that drains out of the Combe d'Ambin. That position explains its later ripening and its austere youth; patient drinkers are rewarded with one of the most complex wines of Chambolle after Les Amoureuses.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 305 m, moderately steep. Thin, stony soil on hard limestone, cooled by air from the Combe d'Ambin.
appellations.nerd_note: Roumier's Les Cras is often its most austere wine in youth, and one of the best agers of the domaine.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Feusselottes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Feusselottes is a 4.4 ha premier cru just east of the village, between Les Chatelots and Les Charmes. The wine is perfumed, fine and red-fruited, a classic mid-slope Chambolle.

It sits on the mid-slope band with Les Chatelots above and Les Charmes and Les Plantes below. Mugneret-Gibourg's version, one of only two premiers crus the Vosne estate makes, has given the climat a following well beyond its modest reputation.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, on brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 4%, and the soil is moderately deep brown limestone-clay, giving a wine that sits between the plush lower slope and the stony upper climats.
appellations.nerd_note: It lies between Les Chatelots and Les Charmes, part of the broad mid-slope band that makes up most of Chambolle's premier cru area.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Fuées
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Fuées sits directly above Bonnes-Mares, at 4.4 ha, on the north side of the Combe d'Ambin. It is Chambolle's most structured premier cru in the north of the village, and its wine resembles a lighter Bonnes-Mares: dark cherry, spice and a firm tannin. Mugnier's Fuées is the benchmark.

With Les Baudes and Les Sentiers it is one of the three premiers crus that touch Bonnes-Mares, and the most highly regarded of them. The soil is thin and stony, so its wines combine Bonnes-Mares' structure with Chambolle's lifted perfume.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 275 to 310 m, moderately steep, with thin soil over hard Bathonian limestone. The lower edge touches the white marl of Bonnes-Mares.
appellations.nerd_note: Mugnier's Fuées is often the darkest wine in its cellar after Musigny and Bonnes-Mares.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Groseilles
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Les Groseilles ('redcurrants') is a 1.4 ha premier cru below the village. The wine is soft, red-fruited and early-drinking, a Chambolle that lives up to its name.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 265 m, nearly flat, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Redcurrant bushes were often planted along vineyard edges in Burgundy, and the name may record such a hedge.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Gruenchers
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Gruenchers is a 2.8 ha premier cru just east of the village, close to Les Chatelots. Dujac and Fourrier both bottle it. The wine is perfumed, red-fruited and silky.

It sits just east of the village among a dense patchwork of small premier crus, with Les Chatelots, Les Groseilles and Les Noirots around it. Fourrier's old-vine Gruenchers and Dujac's version show a silky, perfumed side of Chambolle that sits between the plush lower slope and the austere Cras.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 265 m on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Morey-Saint-Denis has a smaller premier cru with the same name.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Hauts Doix
match: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Hauts Doix
Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Hauts Doix
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Hauts Doix is a 1.7 ha premier cru just north of Les Amoureuses. It shares the same thin, stony soils, and its wines are perfumed and silky with a firmer core. Groffier and Drouhin make the best-known versions.

It shares its neighbour's thin, pebbly soil over hard limestone, with Les Charmes and Les Chabiots alongside. Many tasters find it the closest in style to Amoureuses of all Chambolle's premiers crus, with a little more firmness and a little less flamboyance, at a fraction of the price.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 275 m, on stony limestone soils. Like Les Amoureuses, it has thin soil over fissured hard limestone, and its slight east-southeast tilt gives it good morning sun.
producers: Domaine Robert Groffier Père et Fils
appellations.nerd_note: Groffier's Hauts Doix is often described as the domaine's most underrated wine.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Lavrottes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A small premier cru of 0.92 ha just north of the village, below Les Fuées. Its wine is a firm, perfumed Chambolle premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 275 m on stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below the grand cru Bonnes-Mares, above Les Noirots and Les Gruenchers and beside Les Baudes.
appellations.nerd_note: The name probably comes from *lave*, the flat limestone slabs once used to roof vineyard huts.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Noirots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Les Noirots is a 2.9 ha premier cru below Bonnes-Mares and Les Baudes, near the village. The name suggests dark soil. The wine is a firm, medium-bodied Chambolle premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits between Les Baudes and Les Groseilles, at the point where Chambolle's northern premier crus start to lose the structure that Bonnes-Mares lends them.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Plantes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A 2.6 ha premier cru on the lower slope near Les Charmes. The name refers to new plantings. The wine is a soft, red-fruited Chambolle premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 270 m, gentle slope, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: *Plantes* is a common climat name in Burgundy: it marks land planted to vines later than its neighbours.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Sentiers
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Sentiers lies at the northern edge of Chambolle, at 4.9 ha, just below Bonnes-Mares and next to Morey's La Bussière. It gives a more structured Chambolle than the premier crus near Musigny, with dark fruit and firm tannin.

It sits just below Bonnes-Mares, with Les Baudes to the south and Morey's Les Ruchots and La Bussière across the commune line, on deeper, more clay-rich soil than the southern premier crus. Its wines are darker and firmer than most Chambolle premier crus, a reminder that the north of the village leans toward Morey in style.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with more clay than the southern premier crus.
producers: Domaine Robert Groffier Père et Fils
appellations.nerd_note: Les Sentiers is one of the few Chambolle premier crus to touch Morey-Saint-Denis.

appellations.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Véroilles
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Les Véroilles is a tiny, steep premier cru of 0.42 ha high above Bonnes-Mares, at the edge of the Combe d'Ambin. Only this part of the lieu-dit is premier cru; the rest is village Chambolle. The wine is lean, cool and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 300 to 320 m, slope around 22%. Thin, stony soil over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: It is the highest of Chambolle's premier crus.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Abbaye de Morgeot
match: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Abbaye de Morgeot
Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Abbaye de Morgeot
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Abbaye de Morgeot is the 11.4 ha heart of Morgeot, around the old abbey farm of Maizières. Its best-known wine is the Clos de la Chapelle, a monopole of the Duc de Magenta made by Louis Jadot, in both colours.

It sits in the heart of the Morgeot area, between Morgeot, Les Brussonnes, Les Grands Clos and La Chapelle, on brown limestone-clay with marl. The Duc de Magenta's Clos de la Chapelle, made by Jadot, is the best-known wine, and its reds are among Chassagne's most structured.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. Clay and marl are more abundant here than in the north of the commune, which suits the Pinot Noir still planted in parts of the climat.
producers: Domaine du Duc de Magenta (Louis Jadot)
appellations.nerd_note: The abbey's chapel still stands in the vineyard.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Blanchot dessus
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Blanchot Dessus is a 1.2 ha premier cru directly south of Le Montrachet and next to Criots-Bâtard-Montrachet, the closest premier cru in Chassagne to the great grand cru. The wine is rich and mineral.

It shares the grands crus' band of stony limestone-clay, and its wines are rich and mineral, with something of their density. Darviot-Perrin's version is a rare chance to taste the Montrachet neighbourhood at premier cru prices.
appellations.terroir: South-southwest-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay like the grands crus next door. Its almost flat ground at around 240 m is the same level as the lower part of Le Montrachet, and the soil changes little across the boundary.
appellations.nerd_note: It touches Le Montrachet itself.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Bois de Chassagne
match: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Bois de Chassagne
Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Bois de Chassagne
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Bois de Chassagne is a 13.6 ha premier cru high on the slope toward Santenay, and an umbrella for Les Baudines and Les Embazées. The wines are fresh and mineral, mainly white.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 330 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: The woods (*bois*) that gave it its name still cap the hill.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Cailleret
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Caillerets (Cailleret in the register, with En Cailleret alongside) is one of Chassagne's finest white premier crus, on the slope just south of the village. At 5.6 ha it gives a fine, mineral, floral Chassagne with more tension than Morgeot: citrus, white flowers and a long, stony finish. The umbrella also covers Les Combards and Vigne Derrière.

Vigne Derrière and En Cailleret lie alongside and Les Champs Gain below. Its wines have more tension than Morgeot, and they are often ranked with La Romanée and Les Grandes Ruchottes as Chassagne's finest whites.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 295 m, moderately steep. Stony limestone soils with scree over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Puligny's Le Cailleret, next to Montrachet, shares the name, but the two sites are 2 km apart.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Champs Jendreau
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Champs Jendreau is a 2.1 ha part of La Boudriotte and Morgeot, on the lower slope. The wine is usually blended.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Morgeot and La Boudriotte and beside Les Chaumes.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as La Boudriotte, or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Chassagne
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Chassagne is a 4.1 ha premier cru just south of the village, between La Maltroie and Cailleret. Its name is the village's own.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 280 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Cailleret and Vigne Derrière and above La Maltroie and Les Macherelles.
appellations.nerd_note: The village name is usually derived from Latin *cassanea*, a place of oaks.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean
match: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean
Chassagne-Montrachet 1er Cru Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean
Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean is a 2.0 ha part of the Clos Saint-Jean umbrella, above the village.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Clos Saint-Jean, Chassagne and Les Murées and beside Cailleret.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Clos Saint-Jean.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Clos Chareau
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: The Clos Chareau is a 2.0 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area, at the southern edge of Chassagne.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Grande Borne and beside Morgeot, Les Brussonnes and La Cardeuse.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as Les Brussonnes, or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Clos Pitois
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: The Clos Pitois is a 3.0 ha premier cru at the southern edge of Chassagne, against Santenay. Domaine Roger Belland makes it as a monopole, in red and white.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Santenay's La Comme and Bois de Chassagne, above Les Brussonnes and beside Francemont.
appellations.nerd_note: It may also be sold as Les Brussonnes or Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Clos Saint-Jean
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
The Clos Saint-Jean is a 13.4 ha premier cru above the village, and an umbrella for Les Rebichets, Les Murées and Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean. It has long been known for both colours: Ramonet's red Clos Saint-Jean is a classic, and its whites are fine and mineral.

Les Rebichets and Les Vergers lie to the north and Cailleret to the south. Its wines can be red or white, and Ramonet's red Clos Saint-Jean, firm and red-fruited, is a classic.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Wines from Les Rebichets, Les Murées and Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean may all be sold under the Clos Saint-Jean name.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Dent de Chien
match: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Dent de Chien
Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Dent de Chien
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Dent de Chien ('dog's tooth') is a tiny 0.57 ha premier cru above Le Montrachet, on the Chassagne side. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 240 to 260 m, steep, thin stony soil over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Saint-Aubin's Les Murgers des Dents de Chien lies just above, on the other side of the hill.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru En Cailleret
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: En Cailleret is a 5.1 ha premier cru alongside Cailleret, on the slope just south of the village. The wine is a fine, mineral Chassagne.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 295 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils with scree. On the map it lies above Vigne Derrière, Morgeot and La Boudriotte and beside Cailleret.
appellations.nerd_note: Labels often say simply 'Les Caillerets'.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru En Remilly
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: En Remilly is a small 1.6 ha Chassagne premier cru on the slope above Chevalier-Montrachet, continuing Saint-Aubin's En Remilly. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 280 to 305 m, steep, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above the grand cru Chevalier-Montrachet.
appellations.nerd_note: Most of En Remilly lies in Saint-Aubin.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru En Virondot
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: En Virondot is a steep 2.3 ha premier cru within La Grande Montagne, high above Morgeot. Marc Morey's Virondot is the best-known. The wine is taut and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Very steep, east-southeast-facing at 290 to 330 m, slope around 26%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above La Grande Montagne and En Cailleret.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the steepest premier crus in Chassagne.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Ez Crets
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Ez Crets is a 2.3 ha part of La Maltroie, just south of the village.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Chassagne and beside La Maltroie and Les Places.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as La Maltroie.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Ez Crottes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Ez Crottes is a 2.4 ha part of Morgeot, on the lower slope.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Boudriotte and Abbaye de Morgeot and beside Les Chaumes and Guerchère.
appellations.nerd_note: *Ez* is the old Burgundian form of 'aux'.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Francemont
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Francemont is a 2.4 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Bois de Chassagne, above Les Brussonnes and Les Grands Clos and beside Clos Pitois.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as Les Brussonnes, or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Guerchère
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Guerchère is a 2.2 ha part of Morgeot, on the lowest part of the slope.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 220 to 230 m, almost flat, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Boudriotte and beside Ez Crottes, Les Chaumes and La Chapelle.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Boudriotte
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
La Boudriotte is a 15.6 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area, and itself an umbrella for several smaller climats (Les Chaumes, Les Fairendes, Champs Jendreau, La Roquemaure, Les Petites Fairendes). It is famous for red: Ramonet's Boudriotte rouge is one of the best reds of the Côte de Beaune south of Volnay.

It sits on the gentle slope in the Morgeot area, with Les Fairendes above and Les Chaumes and Champs Jendreau below, on brown limestone-clay. Ramonet's red Boudriotte, deep, firm and long-lived, is a reminder that Chassagne was a red-wine village until the late 20th century.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with more clay than Chassagne's white-wine climats.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold as La Boudriotte or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Cardeuse
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: La Cardeuse is a 0.97 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area. Bernard Moreau makes a red La Cardeuse as a monopole.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Les Boirettes and beside Les Brussonnes, La Grande Borne and Clos Chareau.
appellations.nerd_note: Moreau's La Cardeuse is one of the few single-climat red Chassagnes.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Chapelle
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: La Chapelle is a 4.6 ha premier cru within the Abbaye de Morgeot, around the abbey's chapel. The Duc de Magenta's Clos de la Chapelle lies here.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Abbaye de Morgeot, Morgeot, Les Boirettes and Les Brussonnes.
producers: Domaine du Duc de Magenta (Louis Jadot)
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold as Abbaye de Morgeot or Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Grande Borne
match: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Grande Borne
Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru La Grande Borne
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: La Grande Borne ('the big boundary stone') is a 1.7 ha premier cru at the southern edge of Chassagne, against Santenay's Clos de Tavannes.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 245 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Clos Chareau and beside La Cardeuse, Santenay's Clos de Tavannes and Santenay's Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes.
appellations.nerd_note: The boundary stone probably marked the commune line with Santenay.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Grande Montagne
match: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Grande Montagne
Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru La Grande Montagne
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: La Grande Montagne is a steep 8.3 ha premier cru above Morgeot, below the quarries that give Chassagne its pale, pinkish building stone. It is an umbrella for La Romanée, Les Grandes Ruchottes, En Virondot and Tonton Marcel. The wines are taut and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 255 to 330 m, slope around 24%. Thin stony soil over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: The Chassagne quarries above the vines have supplied building stone for centuries.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Maltroie
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: La Maltroie is a 11.7 ha premier cru just south of the village, and an umbrella for Ez Crets and Les Places. The Château de la Maltroye takes its name from it. The wine is a fine, round Chassagne, in both colours.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The château is spelled with a 'y'; the climat with an 'i'.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Romanée
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Chassagne's La Romanée is a steep 3.4 ha premier cru within La Grande Montagne, above Morgeot. Its whites are among the most mineral and refined of the village, with citrus, white flowers and a stony finish. Paul Pillot and Morey-Coffinet make reference versions.

It sits on the steep slope of La Grande Montagne above Morgeot, with Bois de Chassagne alongside and the old quarries above. The thin soil over hard limestone gives the most mineral, tense Chassagne, and many growers rank it with Les Caillerets and Les Grandes Ruchottes as the village's finest whites.
appellations.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 255 to 320 m, slope around 24%. Thin, stony soil over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: There are three Romanées in Burgundy's classification: the Vosne grand cru, a Gevrey premier cru and this one.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Roquemaure
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: La Roquemaure is a tiny 0.61 ha part of La Boudriotte and Morgeot.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Fairendes and beside La Boudriotte, Vigne Blanche and Les Petites Fairendes.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as La Boudriotte, or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Baudines
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Baudines is a 3.6 ha premier cru within Bois de Chassagne, high above Morgeot. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 285 to 335 m, steep, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above Bois de Chassagne, Les Embazées and Santenay's La Comme.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Bois de Chassagne.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Boirettes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Boirettes is a 2.8 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Morgeot and Les Brussonnes, above La Chapelle and beside Abbaye de Morgeot.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as Les Brussonnes, or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Bondues
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Bondues is a 1.7 ha part of Les Chenevottes, near Blanchot Dessus and the grands crus.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Macherelles and beside Les Chenevottes and Blanchot dessus.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Chenevottes.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Brussonnes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Brussonnes is a 15.8 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area and an umbrella for Clos Chareau, Clos Pitois, Francemont, La Cardeuse, La Grande Borne and Les Boirettes. The wines are generous, red or white.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold as Les Brussonnes or as Morgeot.

Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Champs gain

appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Morgeot and La Boudriotte and beside Champs Jendreau and Ez Crottes.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Chaumées
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Chaumées is a 7.3 ha premier cru above Les Vergers, toward Saint-Aubin. The wine is a fresh, mineral Chassagne.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 265 to 315 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Saint-Aubin's Le Charmois and above Saint-Aubin's Les Combes, Les Vergers and Clos Saint-Jean.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits at the boundary with Saint-Aubin's Les Combes.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Chenevottes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Chenevottes is a 11.0 ha premier cru on the lower slope north of the village, toward Puligny and the grands crus. It is an umbrella for Les Bondues and Les Commes. Its whites are fine and floral, among the best of the northern Chassagne premier crus.

Blanchot Dessus and Les Bondues lie nearby, and its gentle, moderately deep ground gives a rounder white than the steep southern climats. Niellon's and Jean-Noël Gagnard's versions are references.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay over limestone. Its gentle slope, about 4%, and moderately deep soil give a rounder white than the steep upper climats of the south.
appellations.nerd_note: *Chenevottes* refers to hemp (*chanvre*), once grown here.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Combards
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds

appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 285 to 300 m, steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Cailleret, Chassagne, Vigne Derrière and Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Cailleret.

appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Commes is a 1.0 ha part of Les Chenevottes, toward Saint-Aubin.
appellations.terroir: South-southwest-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Saint-Aubin's Les Combes, Saint-Aubin's Les Combes au Sud and Les Vergers and beside Les Chenevottes.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Chenevottes.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Embazées

appellations.summary: Les Embazées is a 5.2 ha premier cru within Bois de Chassagne. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 300 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Bois de Chassagne and Les Baudines and above Morgeot and Les Brussonnes.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Bois de Chassagne.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Fairendes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Fairendes is a 7.1 ha part of La Boudriotte and Morgeot. The wine is a supple Chassagne, red or white.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Grandes Ruchottes and beside Morgeot, La Boudriotte and Les Petits Clos.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as La Boudriotte, or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Grandes Ruchottes
match: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Grandes Ruchottes
Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Grandes Ruchottes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Grandes Ruchottes is a 2.1 ha premier cru within La Grande Montagne, above Morgeot. Ramonet and Paul Pillot make reference versions. The wine is taut, mineral and long-lived.

It sits on the slope of La Grande Montagne below La Grande Montagne itself and above Morgeot and Les Petits Clos, on thin stony soil. Its whites are taut and mineral, with real ageing potential, and Ramonet's Ruchottes is one of the most sought-after premier cru Chassagnes.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 285 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils. The gradient is steep, around 18%, and the soil thin enough that roots reach the fissured limestone quickly, which accounts for the wine's tension.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits on the steep band of thin soil below the old Chassagne quarries, the same band as La Romanée.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Grands Clos
match: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Grands Clos
Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Grands Clos
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Grands Clos is a 3.9 ha part of Morgeot. The wine is a fine Chassagne, red or white.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Tête du Clos, above Abbaye de Morgeot and beside Les Petits Clos and Les Brussonnes.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Morgeot.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Macherelles
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Macherelles is a 5.2 ha premier cru below the village, near Les Chenevottes. The wine is a supple Chassagne.

appellations.nerd_note: It lies at the foot of the slope near the old Route nationale.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Murées

appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Clos Saint-Jean.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Pasquelles
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Pasquelles is a 2.5 ha part of Les Vergers, north of the village.

appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Vergers.

appellations.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Petites Fairendes

Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Petites Fairendes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds

appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside La Boudriotte, Les Petits Clos, Les Fairendes and La Roquemaure.

Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Petits Clos
