appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Les Fourneaux is a 2.8 ha Mercurey premier cru in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu. The red is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 260 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside La Chassière and Les Ruelles.
appellations.nerd_note: Chablis and Savigny also have premier crus named Fourneaux.

appellations.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Montaigus
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Les Montaigus is a 7.7 ha Mercurey premier cru in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu, below the castle of Montaigu. The red is firm and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 295 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus and above Les Velley.
appellations.nerd_note: It lies in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu, the second commune of the Mercurey appellation.

appellations.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Naugues
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Les Naugues is a 4.1 ha Mercurey premier cru. François Raquillet makes it. The red is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Crêts and Clos des Barraults and above Les Vasées and Les Byots.
appellations.nerd_note: Its south-southwest exposure gives good ripeness.

appellations.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Puillets
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Les Puillets is a 8.5 ha Mercurey premier cru. François Raquillet makes it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 280 to 315 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Saumonts.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus of Mercurey.

appellations.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Ruelles
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Les Ruelles is a 2.5 ha Mercurey premier cru in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu. The red is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside Les Fourneaux.
appellations.nerd_note: *Ruelles* are small lanes.

appellations.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Saumonts
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Les Saumonts is a steep 4.1 ha Mercurey premier cru. The red is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: Steep, south-southwest-facing at 290 to 340 m, slope around 24%, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Les Puillets.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus of Mercurey.

appellations.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Vasées
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Les Vasées is a 3.1 ha Mercurey premier cru facing south. The red is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 235 to 250 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Naugues and beside Les Byots and Clos Tonnerre.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits next to the Clos Tonnerre.

appellations.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Velley
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Les Velley is a 10.8 ha Mercurey premier cru. François Raquillet makes it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 300 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus, Les Montaigus and Mercurey Premier Cru Clos du Château de Montaigu and above Le Clos du Roy.
appellations.nerd_note: It lies below the Montaigus climats.

appellations.name: Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus
match: Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: The Clos des Montaigus (registered as 'Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus') is a 5.7 ha premier cru below the ruined medieval castle of Montaigu, mostly in the commune of Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu. The red is firm and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 270 to 310 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl.
appellations.nerd_note: The Clos du Château de Montaigu lies within it.

appellations.name: Mercurey Premier Cru Clos du Château de Montaigu
match: Mercurey Premier Cru Clos du Château de Montaigu
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: The Clos du Château de Montaigu is a 1.9 ha walled Mercurey premier cru within the Clos des Montaigus, below the castle ruins. Domaine du Meix-Foulot makes it as a monopole.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 290 to 315 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus and Les Velley.
appellations.nerd_note: It is the clos closest to the old castle.

appellations.name: Mercurey premier cru Sazenay
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
appellations.summary: Sazenay is a 13.2 ha Mercurey premier cru. The Château de Chamirey and Domaine de Suremain make it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 320 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above La Bondue and La Levrière.
appellations.nerd_note: It is often labelled 'En Sazenay'.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Blagny
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary:
Meursault premier cru Blagny is the umbrella name for white wine from the hamlet of Blagny, high above Meursault and Puligny. It covers 25.0 ha, including La Pièce sous le Bois, Sous le Dos d'Ane, La Jeunellotte, Sous Blagny and Les Ravelles. The wine is taut, cool and mineral, a high-altitude Meursault.

Blagny is a hamlet of a few houses and a chapel, high on the hill between Meursault and Puligny, and its vines sit 50 to 100 m higher than the Côte's great whites. That altitude gives cooler, later-ripening, more mineral wines, which suit a warming climate; Matrot and Martelet de Cherisey are the main local producers.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 360 m, steep in places, with thin marly limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: White from Blagny is Meursault or Puligny premier cru depending on the commune; red is Blagny AOC.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Charmes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Charmes is the largest premier cru of Meursault, about 31 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 31.2 ha), on the gentle lower slope below Perrières and Genevrières, running south to the Puligny boundary. It is split into Charmes Dessus (upper, finer) and Charmes Dessous. The wine is the classic rich Meursault: ripe, round, nutty and buttery, with citrus and a soft, generous texture.

It sits below Les Perrières and Les Genevrières and runs south to touch Puligny's Les Combettes and Les Referts. The upper part, Charmes Dessus, on thinner soil, gives the most refined wines, while Charmes Dessous below is broader and richer. Lafon's and Roulot's Charmes show how much finesse this generous climat can reach.
appellations.terroir: Gentle east-southeast slope at 235 to 255 m. Deeper brown limestone-clay than the upper premier crus.
appellations.nerd_note: *Charmes* comes from *chaume*, fallow ground, not from charm.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Clos des Perrières
match: Meursault premier cru Clos des Perrières
Meursault Premier Cru Clos des Perrières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Perrières is a walled 0.94 ha monopole of Domaine Albert Grivault within the lower part of Les Perrières. Many tasters rank it with the best of Meursault, a dense, mineral, long-lived white.

The clos has a little more clay than Perrières Dessus, and Albert Grivault's wine has the Perrières tension in a slightly broader frame. It is one of the longest-lived Meursaults.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 265 m, gentle slope, thin stony limestone soil with a little clay. The wall around the clos protects it from wind and slightly warms the vines, which may explain its broader texture compared with Perrières Dessus.
appellations.nerd_note: Grivault also makes Pommard Clos Blanc, but the Clos des Perrières is its flagship.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Genevrières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Genevrières lies just north of Les Perrières and above Les Charmes, at about 16.5 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 16.6 ha), split into Genevrières Dessus and Dessous. The name comes from juniper bushes (*genévriers*). Its wine is the most aromatic and floral of the great three Meursault premier crus: white flowers, citrus, spice and a fine, silky texture, less mineral than Perrières but more elegant than Charmes.

Les Genevrières sits between Les Perrières to the south and Le Porusot to the north, with Les Charmes below, and its slightly higher position and thinner soil explain why it is finer than Charmes and more aromatic than Perrières. François Jobard's Genevrières is famous for needing a decade in bottle, and Latour-Giraud, the largest holder, makes a richer, more generous version.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 280 m, moderately steep. Stony limestone soils with a little marl, thinner in Genevrières Dessus.
appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Baudot and Philippe le Bon are both Meursault Genevrières.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru La Jeunellotte
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: La Jeunellotte is a 5.0 ha part of Blagny, high above Meursault. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 325 to 355 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Puligny-Montrachet's Sous le Puits and Les Ravelles and above Blagny and La Pièce sous le Bois.
appellations.nerd_note: Martelet de Cherisey bottles it as 'La Genelotte', the old spelling.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru La Pièce sous le Bois
match: Meursault premier cru La Pièce sous le Bois
Meursault 1er Cru La Pièce sous le Bois
Meursault Premier Cru La Pièce sous le Bois
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary:
La Pièce sous le Bois ('the plot under the woods') is a 11.3 ha part of Blagny, high above Meursault. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru, a fresh, mineral wine.

It sits below the woods at the top of the Blagny slope, above Sous le Dos d'Ane and beside La Jeunellotte, on thin marly limestone. Ampeau's version is classic: taut and mineral, slow to open, with the cool freshness of Blagny's altitude.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 310 to 345 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: The woods above cool the vines and slow ripening.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Le Porusot
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Le Porusot is a 4.4 ha premier cru just south of the village, below Les Bouchères. The wine is a fresh, mineral Meursault, often with a stony edge.

Its wines are tauter and more mineral than most Meursault, closer to Perrières than to Charmes in style, and Roulot's Porusots is a reference.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. The slope steepens here to about 10%, with stony soil that drains fast and keeps yields low.
appellations.nerd_note: Le Porusot and Porusot are listed separately by INAO, but growers usually call the whole area 'Les Porusots' or 'Poruzots'.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Les Bouchères
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Bouchères is a 4.2 ha premier cru just south of the village, above Le Porusot. Roulot makes it. The wine is a fine, mineral Meursault.

Roulot's and Buisson-Charles' versions are fine and mineral, with more tension than the village's broader premiers crus.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the smaller premier crus of Meursault.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Les Caillerets
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Caillerets is a small 1.0 ha Meursault premier cru at the northern end of the commune, against Volnay's Caillerets. Red and white are both made.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Monthélie's Les Champs Fulliots, above Volnay's Santenots and Les Santenots Blancs and beside Volnay's Clos des 60 ouvrées.
appellations.nerd_note: It touches Volnay's Clos des 60 Ouvrées across the commune line.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Les Cras
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Cras is a 3.5 ha premier cru at the northern end of Meursault, next to the Santenots. Red is permitted and sometimes made here as Meursault premier cru rouge, as well as white.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 285 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Volnay's Santenots, Les Plures and Les Santenots Blancs.
appellations.nerd_note: *Cras* means stony ground.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Les Gouttes d'Or
match: Meursault premier cru Les Gouttes d'Or
Meursault Premier Cru Les Gouttes d'Or
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Gouttes d'Or ('drops of gold') is a 5.3 ha premier cru at the northern end of Meursault's premier crus, near the village. The wine is rich and golden, with ripe fruit and spice.

Le Porusot and Les Bouchères lie alongside. Lafon's version is one of the most sought-after Gouttes d'Or, and Arnaud Ente's is among the rarest.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl. The marl in the soil holds water, which helps the vines through dry summers and gives the wine its round texture.
appellations.nerd_note: With Les Bouchères and Le Porusot it forms the group of premier crus just south of the village houses.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Les Plures
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: Les Plures is a 10.4 ha part of the Santenots, in Meursault near Volnay. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru; red is Volnay premier cru Santenots.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Cras and Les Santenots Blancs and beside Volnay's Santenots and Les Santenots du Milieu.
appellations.nerd_note: It is the largest of the three Santenots lieux-dits.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Les Ravelles
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: Les Ravelles is a small 1.2 ha part of Blagny, high above Meursault. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 350 to 380 m, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies above Blagny and Blagny's La Jeunellotte and beside Puligny-Montrachet's Sous le Puits.
appellations.nerd_note: At over 350 m it is one of the highest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Les Santenots Blancs
match: Meursault premier cru Les Santenots Blancs
Meursault Premier Cru Les Santenots Blancs
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: Les Santenots Blancs is a 2.9 ha part of the Santenots, in Meursault but on the Volnay side. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru; red is Volnay premier cru Santenots.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 280 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl.
appellations.nerd_note: The 'Blancs' in the name probably refers to pale soil rather than to white wine.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Les Santenots du Milieu
match: Meursault premier cru Les Santenots du Milieu
Meursault 1er Cru Les Santenots du Milieu
Meursault Premier Cru Les Santenots du Milieu
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary:
Les Santenots du Milieu is a 8.0 ha part of the Santenots, in Meursault near Volnay. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru; red is Volnay premier cru Santenots, the form in which Comtes Lafon makes its famous Volnay-Santenots-du-Milieu.

It sits on the gentle slope at the northern end of Meursault, below Les Santenots Blancs and beside Volnay's En Chevret, on brown limestone-clay. Most of it is planted to Pinot Noir, sold as Volnay-Santenots, but white from here is a fine, round Meursault premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The soil here has more clay than Meursault's southern premier crus, which suits Pinot Noir and explains why red dominates.
appellations.nerd_note: Jacques Prieur's monopole Clos des Santenots is inside it.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Perrières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Perrières is the greatest premier cru of Meursault and the one most often called a grand cru in all but name. It lies at the southern end of the village's slope, against Puligny's Champ Canet and Les Combettes, on stony ground that was once quarried (hence *perrières*). The climat, split into Perrières Dessus and Dessous and including the walled Clos des Perrières, covers 13.3 ha on the INAO delimitation. Dr Lavalle classed it as a *tête de cuvée* in 1855.

Its wine is Meursault's most mineral and tense: less buttery and broad than Charmes, with citrus, white flowers, hazelnut and a stony, almost salty finish that can last for a minute. It ages for 15 to 20 years. Coche-Dury's Perrières is one of the most expensive white wines in Burgundy.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 305 m, moderately steep. Very thin soil over hard limestone and old quarry rubble in Perrières Dessus; a little more clay in Perrières Dessous. The rock is fractured, so roots go deep.
appellations.nerd_note: Coche-Dury's Perrières regularly sells for more than many grands crus, a fair measure of how the market ranks the climat.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Porusot
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Porusot (often spelt Poruzot) is a 7.1 ha premier cru just south of the village, next to Les Genevrières. The wine is a fresh, mineral Meursault.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 280 m, gentle slope, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Bouchères and beside Genevrières and Le Porusot.
appellations.nerd_note: Jobard's Poruzot is often the most austere of its premier crus in youth.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Sous Blagny
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: Sous Blagny is a 2.2 ha part of Blagny, just below the hamlet. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 300 to 335 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Blagny and Blagny's La Jeunellotte and above Sous le Dos d'Ane and Puligny-Montrachet's Les Chalumaux.
appellations.nerd_note: Latour's Château de Blagny is a Meursault-Blagny from here.

appellations.name: Meursault premier cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
match: Meursault premier cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
Meursault 1er Cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
Meursault Premier Cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary:
Sous le Dos d'Ane ('under the donkey's back') is a 5.2 ha part of Blagny, below the hamlet. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru. Domaine Leflaive makes a fine version.

It sits on the Blagny slope below La Pièce sous le Bois and above Meursault's Perrières, on marly limestone. Domaine Leflaive's Sous le Dos d'Ane, from one of Puligny's most famous estates, is a fine, mineral wine that shows how close Blagny's whites can come to Puligny.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 320 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: The 'donkey's back' is presumably the rounded ridge above the climat.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru Champ Toizeau
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Champ Toizeau is a small 1.5 ha Montagny premier cru in Montagny-lès-Buxy.
appellations.terroir: Southwest-facing at 320 to 370 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Chaumelottes and above Les Garchères, Vignes sur le Cloux and Vignes Saint-Pierre.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits next to Les Garchères.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru Chazelle
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Chazelle is a 2.7 ha Montagny premier cru in Jully-lès-Buxy.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 300 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Moullière and Les Coères and beside Les Chaniots.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits below Les Coères.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru Cornevent
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Cornevent is a 3.3 ha Montagny premier cru in Buxy. It lies on the east-southeast-facing slope above the Buxy vineyards.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 275 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. The gradient averages about 12%.
appellations.nerd_note: The name probably points to a windy spot.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru Creux de Beaux Champs
match: Montagny premier cru Creux de Beaux Champs
Montagny 1er Cru Creux de Beaux Champs
Montagny Premier Cru Creux de Beaux Champs
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Creux de Beaux Champs is a 4.5 ha Montagny premier cru in Montagny-lès-Buxy. The white is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 295 to 335 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Beaux Champs, above L'Epaule and beside Les Maroques.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits below Les Beaux Champs.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru L'Epaule
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: L'Epaule ('the shoulder') is a 4.7 ha Montagny premier cru in Montagny-lès-Buxy. The white is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 285 to 330 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Creux de Beaux Champs and Les Maroques and above Les Platières.
appellations.nerd_note: The name describes a shoulder of hillside.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru La Condemine du Vieux Château
match: Montagny premier cru La Condemine du Vieux Château
Montagny 1er Cru La Condemine du Vieux Château
Montagny Premier Cru La Condemine du Vieux Château
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: La Condemine du Vieux Château is a 3.2 ha Montagny premier cru in Buxy, below Le Vieux Château.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 270 to 290 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Le Vieux Château and Les Vignes longues and beside Le Clouzot.
appellations.nerd_note: A *condemine* was the lord's own land, farmed directly rather than let to tenants.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru La Grande Pièce
match: Montagny premier cru La Grande Pièce
Montagny Premier Cru La Grande Pièce
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: La Grande Pièce is a 6.8 ha Montagny premier cru in Buxy. The white is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 315 to 355 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Le Clos Chaudron and above Les Pidances, Les Vignes des Prés and Les Coudrettes.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus of Buxy.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru La Moullière
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: La Moullière is a 4.0 ha Montagny premier cru in Saint-Vallerin.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 285 to 305 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Paquiers, above Chazelle and Les Chaniots and beside Les Coères.
appellations.nerd_note: *Moullière* probably refers to damp ground.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru Le Clos Chaudron
match: Montagny premier cru Le Clos Chaudron
Montagny Premier Cru Le Clos Chaudron
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Le Clos Chaudron is a 5.3 ha Montagny premier cru in Buxy. The white is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 390 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above La Grande Pièce.
appellations.nerd_note: *Chaudron* means cauldron, perhaps for a sheltered bowl in the slope.

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru Le Cloux
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay

appellations.name: Montagny premier cru Les Coères
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Les Coères is the largest and best-known premier cru of Montagny, a 29.8 ha slope that spreads across Montagny-lès-Buxy, Jully-lès-Buxy and Saint-Vallerin. Montagny is a white-only appellation at the southern end of the Côte Chalonnaise; from 1943 to the late 1980s any Montagny reaching 11.5% alcohol could be called premier cru, until growers voluntarily redrew the map and settled on 49 climats on the best mid and upper slopes. Les Coères gives a fresh, citrus and white-flower Chardonnay with a stony finish.

It sits on the gentle slope across three communes, with Les Chaniots, Les Jardins and Les Las around it. Its whites are fresh and mineral, and Aladame's and Feuillat-Juillot's versions are among the best of Montagny.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 260 to 315 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl.
appellations.nerd_note: The 1943 alcohol rule, which tied premier cru to ripeness rather than place, made Montagny a unique case in Burgundy until it was abandoned.

appellations.summary: Les Champs Fulliots is the best-known premier cru of Monthélie, a 7.8 ha climat on the gentle slope that continues Volnay's Clos des Chênes and Clos des 60 Ouvrées across the commune line. Its wines are Volnay's country cousins: perfumed, red-fruited and supple, with a little more earth, and they cost a fraction of the Volnays next door.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 300 m, almost flat at the top of the Volnay slope. Brown limestone-clay with scree, the same strata as the Clos des Chênes. The plateau-like gradient, about 4%, and its position at the top of the Volnay slope give the wine Volnay's finesse with a little more rusticity.
appellations.nerd_note: Monthélie's wines were long sold under the better-known names of Volnay and Pommard, which is one reason the village is still undervalued.

appellations.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Clous
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Clous is a 3.4 ha premier cru on the slope toward Auxey-Duresses, near Les Duresses. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Monthélie.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 270 to 295 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Duresses.
appellations.nerd_note: *Clous* is Burgundian for enclosed plots.

appellations.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Duresses
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Duresses is a 6.6 ha Monthélie premier cru on the east-facing slope toward Auxey-Duresses, continuing Auxey's Les Duresses. The Comtes Lafon make a fine, firm red here. The wine is darker and more structured than the Volnay-side premier crus.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl.
appellations.nerd_note: The climat straddles the Monthélie and Auxey-Duresses boundary.

appellations.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Riottes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Riottes is a 4.0 ha premier cru above the village. The wine is fresh and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 300 to 325 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Le Meix Bataille and beside Les Barbières.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus of Monthélie.

appellations.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Vignes Rondes
match: Monthélie premier cru Les Vignes Rondes
Monthélie Premier Cru Les Vignes Rondes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Vignes Rondes is a 2.7 ha premier cru just above the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Almost flat, southwest exposure at 295 to 305 m, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Le Clos Gauthey and beside Sur la Velle, Le Meix Bataille and Le Cas Rougeot.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits among the cluster of small premier crus around the village.

appellations.name: Monthélie premier cru Sur la Velle
match: Monthélie premier cru Sur la Velle
Monthélie Premier Cru Sur la Velle
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Sur la Velle is a 6.1 ha premier cru just east of the village, beside Volnay's Clos des Chênes. The Château de Monthelie (Domaine de Suremain) makes a reference version. The wine is perfumed and fine.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 300 to 310 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay over limestone.
producers: Château de Monthelie (Domaine Eric de Suremain)
appellations.nerd_note: It lies just above the village, next to the boundary with Volnay's Clos des Chênes.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Aux Charmes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
A tiny premier cru of 1.2 ha at the northern edge of Morey, wedged between Clos de la Roche, Mazoyères-Chambertin and Charmes-Chambertin. It is little seen on its own, and its wine resembles a soft Mazoyères.

It is the only Morey premier cru that touches three grands crus, Clos de la Roche to the west and Mazoyères- and Charmes-Chambertin to the north, at the point where Morey meets Gevrey. Its wines resemble a soft Mazoyères, with dark cherry and spice and a gentle tannin.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 270 m, on brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 4%, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Aux Charmes shares its name, and probably its soils, with Charmes-Chambertin just over the commune boundary.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Aux Cheseaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: A 1.5 ha premier cru at the northern end of Morey, below Charmes-Chambertin. The wine is a fleshy, perfumed premier cru, and Arlaud's version is the best-known.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 260 m, flat, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Charmes-Chambertin and the grand cru Mazoyères-Chambertin and beside Aux Charmes and Clos des Ormes.
appellations.nerd_note: The name, also written Chezeaux, comes from the Latin *casale*, a farmstead.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Clos Baulet
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Clos Baulet is a walled 0.87 ha premier cru a little below Clos des Lambrays, on the village side of the slope. Domaine des Lambrays makes a Clos Baulet from its parcel, a supple, perfumed wine that tastes like a junior version of its grand cru, and Frédéric Magnien makes another.

The clos sits on the village side of the grand cru band, with Clos Sorbè and Les Blanchards alongside, on deeper soil than the Lambrays slope. That deeper soil gives a softer, rounder wine than the grand cru, and the Lambrays and Magnien bottlings make a useful side-by-side lesson in what a few dozen metres and a classification line mean.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Lambrays' bottling is a useful lesson in Burgundian hierarchy: same owner, same cellar, a few dozen metres downslope, one rank lower.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Clos Sorbè
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Clos Sorbè (also written Clos Sorbet) is a walled 3.3 ha premier cru below the village and Clos des Lambrays, next to Les Sorbès. The soils are deeper than those of the grands crus, and the wine is round, fruity and early-drinking for a Morey premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 270 m on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The name comes from the service tree (*sorbier*), once common in Burgundy's field boundaries.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Clos des Ormes
match: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Clos des Ormes
Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru Clos des Ormes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Ormes ('the elms') sits below Clos de la Roche, at 3.1 ha, at the northern end of Morey toward Gevrey. It makes a dark-fruited, structured Morey premier cru, and Georges Lignier is the best-known holder.

The clos lies against the lower edge of Clos de la Roche at the northern end of Morey, with Aux Charmes and Les Charrières on either side. It shares some of the grand cru's dark fruit and structure on deeper, more clay-rich soil, and Georges Lignier's version is the best-known expression.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 270 m, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Elms, like the hemp and service trees in other Morey names, recall a farming landscape before vineyards took over the whole slope.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Côte Rotie
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Morey's Côte Rotie (the 'roasted slope', no relation to the Rhône) is a steep 1.2 ha premier cru directly above Clos des Lambrays and Clos Saint-Denis. The name says it all: a sun-trap on thin, stony soils. The wine is concentrated but fine-boned.

Its thin, rocky ground warms quickly, which is how it got its name. It is the smallest of Morey's high premiers crus, and its wines are concentrated but fine, with the stony finish of the upper slope.
appellations.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 305 to 325 m, slope near 18%. Thin, rocky limestone soils at the top of the grand cru band.
appellations.nerd_note: Its northern Rhône namesake is also a 'roasted' slope: both names describe sun-baked rock rather than any shared history.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru La Bussière
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
La Bussière is the premier cru at the southern edge of Morey, just below Bonnes-Mares and next to Chambolle's Les Sentiers. Its heart is the walled Clos de la Bussière, 2.6 ha in total on the INAO delimitation, which was the property of the Cistercian Abbey of La Bussière-sur-Ouche and has been a monopole of Domaine Georges Roumier since 1953.

Roumier's Clos de la Bussière is a darker, earthier, more masculine wine than its Chambolles: black cherry, spice and a firm, slightly rustic tannin that softens after a decade. It is one of the best values in Roumier's range because the domaine's name rides on its Chambolles.
appellations.terroir: Gentle east-northeast slope at 255 to 265 m. Deeper brown limestone-clay than Chambolle's premier crus, with more clay and iron, which gives the wine its extra structure.
appellations.nerd_note: The clos keeps the name of the abbey that owned it: La Bussière-sur-Ouche, a Cistercian house founded in 1131 in the Ouche valley west of Dijon.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru La Riotte
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
La Riotte is a 2.5 ha premier cru below Clos de la Roche and Clos Saint-Denis, close to the village. It gives a fleshy, fragrant Morey with dark cherry and spice, and in the hands of Perrot-Minot and Taupenot-Merme it is one of the village's more serious premier crus.

La Riotte sits between the village and the grands crus, with Les Millandes and Les Chenevery around it, on slightly gentler ground than Clos de la Roche. Its wines are rounder and earlier than the grand cru, but in old-vine bottlings they gain real depth: dark cherry, spice and a fine, firm finish.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 280 m on brown limestone-clay with some gravel.
appellations.nerd_note: Perrot-Minot's La Riotte comes from old vines and is one of the estate's most consistent premier crus.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Le Village
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: A premier cru of 0.84 ha in the middle of Morey's village, between the houses and Clos des Lambrays. As in several Côte d'Or villages, gardens and plots inside the settlement that had always made good wine were given premier cru status. The wine is a supple Morey premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 270 to 280 m, on brown limestone-clay inside the village.
appellations.nerd_note: Monthélie, Pommard and Volnay also have premier crus called Le Village.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Blanchards
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Blanchards sits on the lower side of the village, below Clos Saint-Denis, at 2.0 ha. Its name probably refers to pale, marly soil. The wine is a fleshy, perfumed Morey premier cru with something of Clos Saint-Denis' red-fruited charm in a smaller frame.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 275 m, on pale limestone-clay with some marl.
appellations.nerd_note: Blanchards, Clos Sorbè and Clos Baulet form a cluster of premier crus on the village side of the grands crus.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Chaffots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Chaffots sits above Clos Saint-Denis and Clos de la Roche, at 2.6 ha, on one of the higher, steeper parts of Morey's slope. The wine is firm and fresh, with red fruit and a mineral spine, lighter than the grands crus below.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 300 to 330 m. Thin stony soil over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: With Les Genavrières and Monts Luisants it forms the band of high premier crus above Morey's grands crus, where the soils thin out and the wines turn leaner.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Charrières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Charrières sits directly below Clos de la Roche, at 2.3 ha. The name refers to a cart track (*charrière*). It is a firm, dark-fruited Morey premier cru that can be excellent in good hands.

It is one of the four premiers crus strung along the grand cru's lower edge, with the Clos des Ormes and Les Faconnières alongside. Its wines share Clos de la Roche's dark fruit, spice and firm structure in a lighter, earlier form, and in good vintages they are among the best values on the Côte de Nuits.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at about 265 m, on brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 4%, with brown limestone-clay a little deeper than in the grand cru.
appellations.nerd_note: Its upper edge touches Clos de la Roche, one of the Côte de Nuits' most underrated grands crus.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Chenevery
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: A 1.9 ha premier cru on the lower slope below Les Millandes, near the Route des Grands Crus. The name recalls hemp fields (*chènevière*). The wine is a fleshy, supple Morey premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 260 m, almost flat, on deep brown clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Hemp was grown widely on the Côte for rope and cloth until the 19th century, and several climats keep the name.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Faconnières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Faconnières lies below Clos de la Roche, at 1.7 ha, between Les Millandes and Les Charrières. It makes a structured, dark-fruited Morey premier cru, close in style to its grand cru neighbour.

Like Les Millandes beside it, Les Faconnières sits on the lower edge of Clos de la Roche, and the two make similar wines: dark-fruited, spicy and firm, with some of the grand cru's iron. Lignier-Michelot's version is the most widely seen.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 265 to 275 m, on brown limestone-clay. Its gradient is gentle, about 4%, and the soil deeper than in Clos de la Roche above, which gives rounder wines.
appellations.nerd_note: Faconnières is one of four premier crus strung along the lower edge of Clos de la Roche, and the most often bottled on its own.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Genavrières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: A small, steep premier cru of 1.1 ha above Clos de la Roche, between Les Chaffots and Monts Luisants. The name refers to juniper (*genièvre*) that grew on these dry slopes. Its wine is lean, firm and stony, in the style of Morey's high climats.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 305 to 335 m. Thin, rocky limestone soil with little clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Its lower edge touches Clos de la Roche, but at this height the soil is much thinner and the wine far more austere.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Gruenchers
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: A small premier cru of 0.51 ha just below the village, near Les Blanchards. It shares its name with a better-known Chambolle premier cru a short way south. The wine is a perfumed, medium-bodied Morey.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in Morey, and its wine usually disappears into premier cru blends.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Millandes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Millandes sits below Clos de la Roche, at 4.2 ha, and is one of Morey's larger and better-known premier crus. The wine has Clos de la Roche's dark fruit and structure in a softer, earlier form, with a hint of earth and spice.

Les Millandes sits just below Clos de la Roche and Clos Saint-Denis, next to Les Faconnières and La Riotte, and it is one of the most reliable of Morey's lower premier crus. Arlaud and Pierre Amiot both make it in a dark, spicy style that shows its grand cru neighbour's influence.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with Bajocian marl at depth.
appellations.nerd_note: Millandes, Faconnières, Charrières and Clos des Ormes form a row of premier crus directly below Clos de la Roche.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Ruchots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Ruchots lies just below Clos de Tart and the Morey section of Bonnes-Mares, at 2.6 ha. It is one of Morey's finest premier crus, with the perfume of Chambolle and the structure of Morey: dark cherry, violet and a firm, fine tannin. Arlaud's Ruchots is the benchmark.

Its position, wedged below Clos de Tart and Bonnes-Mares at the southern edge of Morey, gives it the deepest pedigree of Morey's lower premier crus. It shows what separates Morey from Chambolle next door: a little more earth, spice and grip under the same red-fruited perfume.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 270 m, on brown limestone-clay with more stones than the lower Morey premier crus.
appellations.nerd_note: Its neighbour across the commune border, Chambolle's Les Sentiers, makes a similar wine with a little less structure.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Sorbès
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Sorbès is a 2.7 ha premier cru on the southern side of the village, next to the Clos Sorbè. It gives a supple, perfumed Morey with soft tannin.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Clos Sorbè.
appellations.nerd_note: Les Sorbès and Clos Sorbè share the same etymology, the service tree.

appellations.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Monts Luisants
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Monts Luisants, the 'shining hills', is the highest and steepest premier cru in Morey, climbing above Clos de la Roche toward the woods; the name is usually explained by the way the sun catches the pale limestone. At 5.4 ha it is a cool site that gives the most mineral wines of the village, in both colours.

It is famous above all for white. In 1911 the Ponsot family planted Aligoté here, and for decades their Clos des Monts Luisants blanc was the only premier cru on the Côte made from Aligoté, a quirk of history the rules tolerated. Dujac makes a Chardonnay-based Morey premier cru blanc from the site, and several growers make a taut, high-toned red with red cherry and crushed stone.
appellations.terroir: Very steep, east-southeast-facing at 305 to 360 m, slope often above 24%. Thin, stony soils on hard Bathonian limestone at the top of the slope, with marl patches that suit white grapes.
appellations.nerd_note: Ponsot's 1911 Aligoté vines are among the oldest productive vines on the Côte de Nuits.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Argillas
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Aux Argillas is a 1.6 ha premier cru just north of the town, named for its clay. The wine is a soft, early-drinking Nuits premier cru.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, clay-limestone soils. On the map it lies below Aux Thorey and beside Aux Bousselots.
appellations.nerd_note: Not to be confused with the Clos des Argillières in Prémeaux, at the other end of the appellation.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Boudots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Aux Boudots is the northernmost premier cru of Nuits, at 6.4 ha, adjoining Vosne's Malconsorts. Its wines have Vosne's perfume and Nuits' structure: dark cherry, violet and spice, with a polished tannin. Méo-Camuzet, Grivot and Leroy make the reference versions.

It touches Vosne's Malconsorts across the commune line, with Les Damodes above and Aux Cras to the south, on stony brown limestone over hard rock. Méo-Camuzet's Boudots is one of the domaine's best values, and Leroy's shows the dense, spicy richness that northern Nuits can reach.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony brown limestone over hard rock. The gradient is about 15%, steeper than the southern Nuits premier crus, and the stony soil gives good drainage.
appellations.nerd_note: It is often described as the Vosne of Nuits.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Bousselots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Aux Bousselots is a 4.2 ha premier cru just north of the town, on the gentle lower slope. Robert Chevillon's version is well known. The wine is fleshy and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Aux Chaignots and Aux Thorey and beside Aux Argillas.
appellations.nerd_note: Bousselots is one of the more affordable of Chevillon's premier crus.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Chaignots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Aux Chaignots is a 5.8 ha premier cru just north of the town, on the slope above Aux Vignerondes. Mugneret-Gibourg, Chevillon and Faiveley make fine versions. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.

It sits on the slope just north of the town, below Les Damodes and beside Aux Murgers and Aux Thorey, on stony limestone-clay. Its wines combine the perfume of the northern premier crus with more grip than Aux Murgers; Mugneret-Gibourg's version is the most sought-after.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 280 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Mugneret-Gibourg makes only two premier crus: this one and Chambolle's Les Feusselottes.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Champs Perdrix
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Champs Perdrix
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Aux Champs Perdrix
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Aux Champs Perdrix is a steep 1.4 ha premier cru above Aux Chaignots, north of the town. The wine is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 265 to 295 m, thin stony soil. On the map it lies below En la Perrière Noblot and above Aux Chaignots and Aux Thorey.
appellations.nerd_note: It shares the partridge name with Aux Perdrix, at the opposite end of the appellation.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Cras
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Aux Cras is a 3.0 ha premier cru just south of Aux Boudots, on the northern slope of Nuits. The wine is fine and perfumed, with Vosne's influence.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below La Richemone and Les Damodes, above Aux Murgers and beside Aux Boudots.
appellations.nerd_note: *Cras* means stony ground.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Murgers
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Aux Murgers is a 4.9 ha premier cru north of the town, below Aux Cras. *Murgers* are the stone heaps cleared from the vineyard. Méo-Camuzet and Cathiard both make fine versions: perfumed, dark-fruited and silky.

It sits on the gentle slope north of the town, with La Richemone above, Aux Chaignots alongside and Aux Vignerondes below. Its wines are among the most perfumed of Nuits, with the silky tannin of the northern premier crus rather than the iron grip of Saint-Georges.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. The stone heaps (*murgers*) that give the climat its name are still visible in places at the edge of the vines.
appellations.nerd_note: Cathiard's Aux Murgers is often its most approachable premier cru.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Perdrix
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Aux Perdrix ('the partridges') is a 3.4 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, above the Clos des Corvées. Most of it belongs to Domaine des Perdrix, which makes a dense, dark-fruited wine.

It sits above the Clos des Corvées and below Les Terres Blanches in Prémeaux, on stony limestone-clay with good drainage. The Devillard family's Domaine des Perdrix, which also owns the Château de Chamirey in Mercurey, makes a dark, concentrated, modern-style wine from it.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The domaine takes its name from the climat, its main holding.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Thorey
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Aux Thorey is a 5.7 ha premier cru just north of the town, near the mouth of the Meuzin valley. Sylvain Cathiard's version is well known. The wine is fresh and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 285 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Aux Champs Perdrix, above Aux Argillas and Aux Bousselots and beside Aux Chaignots.
appellations.nerd_note: It is the closest premier cru to the town of Nuits.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Vignerondes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Aux Vignerondes is a 3.9 ha premier cru just north of the town, below Aux Chaignots. The wine is a soft, fruity Nuits premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Aux Chaignots and beside Aux Murgers.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the lower premier crus on the northern side of Nuits.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Chaines Carteaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Chaines Carteaux is a steep 2.5 ha premier cru above Les Saint-Georges, near Les Vaucrains. Gouges makes it, and the wine is firm, dark-fruited and stony.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 260 to 320 m, slope around 25%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above Les Vaucrains, Les Saints-Georges and Les Didiers and beside Les Terres Blanches.
appellations.nerd_note: Its lower edge looks down onto Les Saint-Georges, about 30 m below.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Château Gris
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Château Gris is a terraced, walled 2.8 ha premier cru above the town, crowned by a small château. It is a monopole of Lupé-Cholet, owned by Albert Bichot. The wine is supple and perfumed, with red fruit.

The terraced clos sits above the town on the slope south of the Meuzin valley, with Les Crots and Rue de Chaux below. Its steep, stony terraces give a lighter, more perfumed wine than the premier crus on the lower slope.
appellations.terroir: Steep, terraced, east-facing at 260 to 300 m, slope around 26%. Thin stony soil over hard limestone. The terraces were built to hold soil on a slope that averages about 26%, among the steepest in Nuits.
appellations.nerd_note: Its stone terraces are a rarity on the Côte de Nuits, looking more like a Rhône hillside than Burgundy.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos Arlot
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
The Clos de l'Arlot is a walled 4.0 ha monopole of Domaine de l'Arlot in Prémeaux, surrounding the estate buildings. It makes both red and white: the white, mainly Chardonnay, from a pale, marly upper terrace, is one of the few serious whites of the Côte de Nuits.

The clos lies at the foot of the Prémeaux slope, around the estate's buildings, with the Clos de la Maréchale to the south. Its red is perfumed and fine, but the white, from a marly terrace in the upper clos, is the more unusual wine: a citrus-scented, mineral white from the heart of red-wine country.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 220 to 260 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils with a terrace of white marl.
appellations.nerd_note: The clos sits just north of the Clos de la Maréchale, so two of Prémeaux's three big walled monopoles are neighbours.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos Saint-Marc
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: The Clos Saint-Marc is a 0.92 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, a monopole of Domaine Michèle et Patrice Rion. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 250 m, gentle slope, clay-limestone soils. On the map it lies below Clos des Argillières and beside Clos des Corvées Pagets.
appellations.nerd_note: It lies within the larger Argillières area of Prémeaux.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos de la Maréchale
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos de la Maréchale
Nuits-Saint-Georges 1er Cru Clos de la Maréchale
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Clos de la Maréchale
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
The Clos de la Maréchale is one of the largest monopoles in the Côte d'Or, at 9.6 ha, in Prémeaux at the southern end of Nuits. It belongs to the Mugnier family: Faiveley leased and made it from 1950 until 2003, and since the 2004 vintage Frédéric Mugnier has made it himself.

It is a lower-slope site with deeper soils, and Mugnier's red is a supple, fragrant Nuits with red cherry and spice, much lighter than Faiveley's old style. He also makes a small amount of white from Chardonnay planted in the clos.
appellations.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 240 to 255 m. Deep brown limestone-clay over Prémeaux limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Mugnier's Maréchale is the best-value wine in an estate otherwise known for Musigny and Amoureuses.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Argillières
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Argillières
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Clos des Argillières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: The Clos des Argillières is a 4.1 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, named for its clay (*argile*). Daniel Rion and Patrice Rion both make it; the wine is dark and firm.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 270 m, moderately steep, clay-limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Clay content is higher here than in most Nuits premier crus, which gives fuller, rounder wines.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Corvées
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Corvées
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Clos des Corvées
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Corvées is a 5.2 ha monopole of Prieuré-Roch in Prémeaux. *Corvées* were the feudal labour tenants owed their lord. Prieuré-Roch makes a dark, wild, whole-cluster red from it.

It sits on the gentle slope in the middle of Prémeaux, with Aux Perdrix above, the Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges to the north and the Clos des Corvées Pagets alongside. Prieuré-Roch's whole-bunch, low-sulphur style, inherited from Henri-Frédéric Roch, makes it one of the most distinctive wines of the Côte de Nuits.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 9%, and the soil a brown limestone-clay with white oolite pebbles typical of Prémeaux.
appellations.nerd_note: Henri-Frédéric Roch, of the family that co-owns the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, founded Prieuré-Roch in 1988.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Corvées Pagets
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Corvées Pagets
Nuits-Saint-Georges 1er Cru Clos des Corvées Pagets
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Clos des Corvées Pagets
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: The Clos des Corvées Pagets is a 1.6 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, beside the Clos des Corvées. Arnoux-Lachaux is the best-known holder. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with white oolite pebbles. On the map it lies below Clos des Argillières and Les Argillières and beside Clos des Corvées and Clos Saint-Marc.
appellations.nerd_note: It was carved out of the larger Aux Corvées lieu-dit.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges
Nuits-Saint-Georges 1er Cru Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges is a 7.2 ha monopole of Domaine de l'Arlot in Prémeaux, next to Les Didiers. It is the estate's flagship red: perfumed, red-fruited and fine, more elegant than most Nuits premier crus.

The clos sits in the northern part of Prémeaux, with Les Didiers and Aux Perdrix around it and the Clos des Corvées below. Its wines show the finer, more perfumed side of the Prémeaux premier crus, and Arlot's biodynamic farming since the early 2000s has made them more precise and less extracted than in the past.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay. The hard pink Prémeaux limestone lies close beneath the vines here, as in Les Saint-Georges next door.
appellations.nerd_note: Arlot has been owned by AXA Millésimes since 1987 and farmed biodynamically since 2003.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Grandes Vignes
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Grandes Vignes
Nuits-Saint-Georges 1er Cru Clos des Grandes Vignes
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Clos des Grandes Vignes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: The Clos des Grandes Vignes is a 2.2 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, the only Nuits premier cru below the main road (D974). It was bought in 2012 by Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair, which makes it as a monopole. Both red and white are made.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 220 to 235 m, gentle slope, iron-rich clay-limestone with sand.
appellations.nerd_note: Liger-Belair paid about 3 million euros for it in 2012, from the Château de Puligny-Montrachet, which had bought it from Thomas-Moillard.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges is a walled 3.6 ha monopole of Domaine Henri Gouges within Les Porrets, just south of the town. Gouges' wine is darker and firmer than its Les Cailles, with black fruit and earth, and is one of the best values among serious Nuits premier crus.

The clos sits on the gentle slope just south of the town, next to Les Porrets-Saint-Georges and Roncière, with Les Perrières above. Gouges has owned it for generations, and its wine is the estate's most affordable premier cru: firm, dark and earthy, with the house's typical slow evolution.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The 'Saint-Georges' tacked onto Porrets is a reminder of how much prestige the great vineyard next door has always carried.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru En la Perrière Noblot
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru En la Perrière Noblot
Nuits-Saint-Georges 1er Cru En la Perrière Noblot
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru En la Perrière Noblot
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: En la Perrière Noblot is a small 0.64 ha premier cru high above Aux Chaignots, on stony ground once quarried. Machard de Gramont and Alain Michelot make it.
appellations.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 275 to 300 m, slope around 20%, thin stony soil.
appellations.nerd_note: Like several Nuits climats, its name records an old quarry (*perrière*) and, probably, a former owner.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru La Richemone
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: La Richemone is a 2.2 ha premier cru north of the town, above Aux Murgers. Perrot-Minot and Alain Michelot make well-known versions. The wine is deep and spicy.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Damodes and above Aux Murgers, Aux Cras and Aux Chaignots.
appellations.nerd_note: Perrot-Minot's 'Ultra' bottling comes from very old vines here.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Argillières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: A tiny 0.24 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, beside the Clos des Argillières. Its wine is usually blended.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, steep, clay-limestone soils. On the map it lies above Clos des Corvées Pagets, Clos Arlot and Clos des Corvées and beside Clos des Argillières.
appellations.nerd_note: At under a third of a hectare it is one of Nuits' smallest premier crus.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Cailles
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Cailles lies just north of Les Saint-Georges, at 3.8 ha, on the gentle lower slope. The name may refer to quail (*cailles*) or to stones. It is the most elegant of the great trio south of the town (with Saint-Georges and Vaucrains): perfumed, red-fruited and silky, with Nuits' structure in a finer frame.

Les Porrets and Les Vaucrains lie alongside. Robert Chevillon's old-vine Cailles is the reference and shows why many tasters place Les Cailles just behind Saint-Georges and Vaucrains in the Nuits hierarchy.
appellations.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 245 to 260 m, on stony brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Chevillon's Les Cailles comes from old vines and is often the first of its big three (with Saint-Georges and Vaucrains) to open.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Chabœufs
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Chabœufs is a 2.8 ha premier cru above Les Cailles and next to Les Vaucrains. Jean-Jacques Confuron's version is well known. The wine is dark-fruited and firm.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 280 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits between Les Vaucrains and Les Perrières, where the slope begins to steepen toward the woods.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Crots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Crots (hollows) is a 1.1 ha premier cru above Les Pruliers, close to the town. The wine is a firm, mid-weight Nuits premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Château Gris, above Les Pruliers and Les Procès and beside Les Hauts Pruliers.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits just below the Château Gris terraces.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Damodes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Damodes is a large, steep 8.8 ha premier cru at the top of the slope north of Nuits, adjoining Vosne. The wine is fresh and lean, with red fruit and mineral tension.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 280 to 335 m, slope around 22%, thin stony soil over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Its upper edge touches the woods at more than 330 m.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Didiers
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Didiers is a 2.4 ha premier cru at the Prémeaux boundary, just south of Les Saint-Georges. It is a monopole of the Hospices de Nuits, sold at the Hospices' March auction. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.

The Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges lies alongside and Les Terres Blanches above. Every barrel is sold at the Hospices de Nuits auction to a négociant or private buyer, who finishes and bottles it.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay. The gradient is moderate, about 12%, on stony limestone-clay like Les Saint-Georges.
appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Nuits auction is the smaller cousin of the Beaune sale, held each March.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Hauts Pruliers
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Hauts Pruliers
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Les Hauts Pruliers
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.19 ha above Les Pruliers, on a steep strip at the top of the slope. Its wine is usually blended with Les Pruliers or into a Nuits premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 265 to 275 m, thin stony soil.
appellations.nerd_note: At around a fifth of a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus on the Côte de Nuits.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Perrières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Perrières sits above Les Porrets and Les Cailles, at 3.3 ha, on stony ground once quarried. It is best known for white: Henri Gouges' 'La Perrière' blanc comes from a white-berried mutation of Pinot Noir found in a Gouges vineyard in the 1930s and propagated here, now known as Pinot Gouges.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 280 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Gouges' white is one of very few Côte de Nuits whites made from a mutation of Pinot Noir rather than from Chardonnay.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Porrets-Saint-Georges
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Porrets-Saint-Georges lies just north of Les Cailles, at 3.5 ha. The name probably refers to wild leeks (*porrets*). The wine is a structured, dark-fruited Nuits premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, stony brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Perrières and Les Chabœufs and beside Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges and Les Cailles.
appellations.nerd_note: Henri Gouges' walled Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges, registered as a separate premier cru name, sits alongside.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Poulettes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Poulettes is a steep 2.1 ha premier cru high above Les Perrières, south of the town. The wine is firm and fresh, with red fruit.
appellations.terroir: Steep, south-southeast-facing at 270 to 300 m, slope around 26%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above Les Chabœufs and Les Perrières and beside Les Vallerots.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the highest and steepest premier crus in Nuits.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Procès
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Procès is a 1.4 ha premier cru at the southern edge of the town, below Les Crots. The name may recall a lawsuit over the land. The wine is a soft, early-drinking Nuits premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Its neighbours Rue de Chaux and Les Pruliers complete the cluster of premier crus at the town's southern edge.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Pruliers
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Pruliers lies just south of the town, at 7.7 ha, below Les Crots and next to Roncière. It makes a dense, firm, earthy Nuits premier cru with dark fruit and a structured tannin. Gouges, Chevillon and Grivot are major growers.

It sits just south of the town, between Les Crots above and Roncière, Les Procès and Rue de Chaux around it, on stony brown soil that gives some of the darkest, firmest wines of the southern half of the appellation. Gouges' Pruliers is one of the domaine's most structured wines.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, stony brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 8%, and the stony brown soil holds enough iron to give the wine its dark colour.
appellations.nerd_note: The name probably refers to wild plum or sloe bushes (*prunelliers*).

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Saints-Georges
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Saint-Georges (Les Saints-Georges in the register) is the vineyard that gave Nuits its name: the town added 'Saint-Georges' in 1892. It lies just north of the Prémeaux boundary, at about 7.5 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 7.5 ha). When the appellations were drawn in 1936 Nuits ended up with no grand cru at all; the story goes that Henri Gouges, the leading grower of the day, declined to press the vineyard's case.

Since 2007 the growers, led by Thibault Liger-Belair (the largest owner, with just over 2 ha), have campaigned to have it promoted, and the application has been with the INAO for well over a decade. Most observers expect it to become Nuits' first grand cru eventually.

The wine is the most complete of Nuits: deep in colour, with black cherry, iron, spice and a firm but polished tannin that needs ten years. It is more refined than Les Vaucrains above it and denser than Les Cailles to the north.
appellations.terroir: Gentle east-southeast slope at 240 to 260 m. Stony brown limestone-clay over hard Prémeaux limestone, with gravel washed down from the slope above; the soil is shallow and drains well.
appellations.nerd_note: About 13 owners share the vineyard, and all of them had to agree a common production rulebook before the grand cru file could go forward.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Terres Blanches
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Terres Blanches
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Les Terres Blanches
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Terres Blanches is a steep 4.3 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, above Aux Perdrix. The name ('white earths') refers to pale marl soil, and it is one of the few Nuits climats that makes a significant white wine.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 265 to 305 m, slope around 23%, pale marly limestone soil.
appellations.nerd_note: The pale marl that gives it its name suits Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc better than most Nuits soils.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Vallerots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Vallerots is a 0.88 ha premier cru at the top of the slope above Les Vaucrains. The wine is a lean, mineral Nuits premier cru.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 275 to 300 m, thin soil over hard limestone. On the map it lies above Les Chabœufs and Les Vaucrains and beside Les Poulettes.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest and highest premier crus south of the town.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Vaucrains
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Vaucrains lies above Les Saint-Georges, at 6.2 ha, on steeper and stonier ground, and is often ranked second in Nuits. The name is usually glossed as 'valley of poor soil', and the wine is the most muscular of the village: dense, dark, iron-laden, with firm tannin that needs a decade or more. Gouges and Chevillon make the reference versions.

Its stony soil and steeper slope above Les Saint-Georges give the most tannic and long-lived wines of Nuits, and Gouges' and Chevillon's versions routinely need 15 years to open fully. Where Saint-Georges is complete and polished, Vaucrains is wilder, more angular and more mineral, and the two make the classic Nuits comparison.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 290 m, steeper than Les Saint-Georges. Thin, stony soil with limestone rubble over Prémeaux limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Vaucrains is a good example of a Burgundy rule of thumb: the steeper, stonier site above often makes the more tannic wine, the gentler slope below the more complete one.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Roncière
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Roncière (bramble ground) is a 2.1 ha premier cru just south of the town, between Les Pruliers and the Clos des Porrets. Robert Chevillon's Roncière is the best-known; the wine is fleshy and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the smaller climats in Chevillon's range of eight Nuits premier crus.

appellations.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Rue de Chaux
match: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Rue de Chaux
Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Rue de Chaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Rue de Chaux is a 2.1 ha premier cru just south of the town; the name probably refers to lime (*chaux*). The wine is a fleshy, red-fruited Nuits premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits at the foot of the Château Gris slope, part of the cluster of small premier crus at the town's southern edge.

appellations.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Clos Berthet
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: The Clos Berthet is a 1.2 ha white premier cru high above Pernand village, a monopole of Domaine P. Dubreuil-Fontaine. The wine is a fresh, mineral Chardonnay.
appellations.terroir: Steep, west-southwest-facing at 310 to 345 m, slope around 23%, on thin marl and limestone. The west-southwest exposure is unusual for a Côte d'Or premier cru.
producers: Domaine P. Dubreuil-Fontaine Père et Fils
appellations.nerd_note: Its west-facing slope catches the afternoon sun, which helps the white ripen at this altitude.

appellations.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Creux de la Net
match: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Creux de la Net
Pernand-Vergelesses 1er Cru Creux de la Net
Pernand-Vergelesses Premier Cru Creux de la Net

appellations.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru En Caradeux
