appellations.summary:
En Caradeux is a 14.5 ha premier cru on the slope above Pernand village, facing east. Jadot's Clos de la Croix de Pierre is inside it. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Pernand, and white is also made.

En Caradeux sits on the east-facing slope above Pernand village, with Creux de la Net and the Ile des Vergelesses below. It makes both colours, and Jadot's walled Clos de la Croix de Pierre, inside it, is the best-known wine: a firm, red-fruited Pernand with good ageing potential.

appellations.nerd_note: Jadot's Clos de la Croix de Pierre is one of the few walled clos in Pernand.

appellations.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Ile des Vergelesses

Pernand-Vergelesses Premier Cru Ile des Vergelesses
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
The Ile des Vergelesses is the finest red of Pernand-Vergelesses, a 9.4 ha premier cru on the slope that faces Savigny across the valley. It gives a fine, perfumed red with red fruit and a firm, mineral finish, often compared with a light Corton.

It touches Pernand's Les Vergelesses and En Caradeux and, across the boundary, Savigny's Les Vergelesses and Les Basses Vergelesses. Its iron-rich soils give a more structured red than most of Pernand, and Chandon de Briailles' version is a benchmark for the village.

appellations.nerd_note: It is the Pernand premier cru that growers most often compare with Corton, and it is usually the most expensive red of the village.

appellations.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Sous Frétille
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary:
Sous Frétille is a 10.3 ha white-only premier cru high on the slope above Pernand village, on the west side of the hill of Corton. It gives a taut, mineral Chardonnay with Corton-Charlemagne's cut at a fraction of the price.

It sits high on the western flank of the hill of Corton, on the same band of white marl that gives Corton-Charlemagne its tension, but facing south toward the grand cru across a little valley. Its whites are lean, citrus-driven and mineral, slower to open than most village whites, and they age well for a decade.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 300 to 365 m, steep, on thin white marl and limestone. At 300 to 365 m, with a median gradient near 24%, it is one of the highest and steepest premier crus of the Côte de Beaune.
producers: Domaine P. Dubreuil-Fontaine Père et Fils
appellations.nerd_note: It faces south toward Corton-Charlemagne across a small valley.

appellations.name: Pommard premier cru Clos des Epeneaux
match: Pommard premier cru Clos des Epeneaux
Pommard Premier Cru Clos des Epeneaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Epeneaux is a walled 5.2 ha monopole of Domaine du Comte Armand, within the Epenots at the northern end of Pommard, in the family since the early 19th century. Under Pascal Marchand (1985 to 1999) and Benjamin Leroux (1999 to 2014) it became the most consistent great Pommard: dense, dark and spicy, with a firm, polished tannin. The estate farms biodynamically.

The clos sits on the gentle lower slope between Les Petits Epenots and Les Grands Epenots, on deep, gravelly brown soil that drains well. Comte Armand's wines are dense and spicy in youth and need ten years or more; they show that the Epenots, not only the Rugiens, can make Pommard of real depth.
appellations.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 240 to 250 m. Brown limestone-clay with gravel, over Bathonian limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: At over 5 ha it is the largest monopole in Pommard.

appellations.nerd_note: It runs into Volnay's Frémiets across the commune line.

appellations.name: Pommard premier cru Les Grands Epenots
match: Pommard premier cru Les Grands Epenots
Pommard Premier Cru Les Grands Epenots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Grands Epenots lies on the gentle lower slope at the northern end of Pommard, toward Beaune, at 10.1 ha. With Les Petits Epenots and the Clos des Epeneaux it forms the Epenots, which Pommard's growers proposed for grand cru with Rugiens in the 2010s. The wine is the most elegant side of Pommard: perfumed, red- and black-fruited, with a silkier tannin than Rugiens.

Domaine de Courcel's Grand Clos des Epenots, about 5 ha within the climat, is the reference.

The Clos des Epeneaux, Les Petits Epenots and La Refène lie around it. The Epenots and the Rugiens have long been regarded as Pommard's two greatest climats; Lavalle in 1855 rated both at the top.
appellations.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 240 to 255 m. Deeper brown limestone-clay with gravel and some iron, less red than Rugiens.
appellations.nerd_note: The Epenots are usually said to take their name from thorny bushes (*épines*) that once grew on this ground.

appellations.name: Pommard premier cru Les Jarolières

Les Jarolières is a 3.2 ha premier cru at the southern end of Pommard, against Volnay's Frémiets. Pousse d'Or and Jean-Marc Boillot make it. The wine is perfumed and fine, a Pommard with Volnay's grace.

It runs into Volnay's Frémiets. Its wines have Pommard's structure with Volnay's perfume, and Pousse d'Or's and Jean-Marc Boillot's versions are among the most elegant Pommards.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 280 m, moderately steep, red limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits just below Les Rugiens on the Volnay side.

Les Petits Epenots is the larger half of the Epenots, at 15.1 ha, on the lower slope at the northern end of Pommard against the Beaune boundary. Most of the Clos des Epeneaux lies within it. The wine is perfumed and supple, a little lighter than Grands Epenots.

Les Pézerolles and Les Saussilles lie above it, and the Clos des Epeneaux occupies much of it. Its wines are perfumed and supple, the elegant side of Pommard.

appellations.name: Pommard premier cru Les Pézerolles
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Pézerolles sits above the Epenots, at 5.9 ha, near the Beaune boundary. Its wine is firmer and more mineral than the Epenots, with red fruit and a lean, elegant structure. De Montille's Pézerolles is a reference.

Les Charmots lies above it. De Montille's and Lafarge's versions show Pommard's more refined side.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. The gradient steepens here to about 12%, and the soil thins toward the top, which is why the wine is leaner than the Epenots below.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits above the Epenots at the Beaune end of the village, where the slope begins to steepen.

appellations.name: Pommard premier cru Les Rugiens Bas
match: Pommard premier cru Les Rugiens Bas
Pommard Premier Cru Les Rugiens Bas
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Rugiens Bas is the most famous premier cru in Pommard, and with the Epenots it is one of the two climats that Pommard's growers asked the INAO to promote to grand cru in the 2010s. The name comes from the red (*rouge*) colour of the iron-rich soil, and the lower half of the climat, 5.8 ha on the INAO delimitation, is regarded as the better part.

Its wine is Pommard at full strength but with polish: deep in colour, with black cherry, plum, iron and spice, and a firm, dense tannin that needs ten years or more. Compared with the Epenots it is more structured and mineral; compared with the Rugiens Hauts above, riper and denser. Jules Lavalle rated it the best of Pommard in 1855.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 255 to 280 m, moderately steep, just south of the village toward Volnay. Red, iron-rich clay with limestone scree over Bathonian limestone; the iron oxides give the soil its colour.
appellations.nerd_note: Pommard has no grand cru, and Rugiens Bas is usually the first name mentioned when growers make the case for one.

appellations.name: Pommard premier cru Les Rugiens Hauts
match: Pommard premier cru Les Rugiens Hauts
Pommard Premier Cru Les Rugiens Hauts
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Rugiens Hauts is the upper half of the Rugiens, at 6.8 ha, rising toward Volnay's Pitures. The soil is thinner and stonier than in Rugiens Bas, and the wine is a little lighter and fresher, with red fruit and a mineral, firm tannin.

It sits above Les Rugiens Bas toward Volnay's Pitures Dessus, on thinner, stonier soil than the lower half. The wines are lighter, more mineral and more perfumed than Rugiens Bas, and in warm vintages they can be the better balanced of the two.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 315 m, moderately steep, thin red limestone soils with scree. The gradient averages about 14%, steeper than in Rugiens Bas, and the stony scree drains fast.
appellations.nerd_note: Many labels just say 'Rugiens' and blend the two halves.

appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: En Servy is a 4.0 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 285 to 335 m, steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above La Frérie and beside Au Vignerais.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits next to Au Vignerais.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru La Frérie
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: La Frérie is a 4.1 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly. The wine is ripe and fine.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies below Au Vignerais and En Servy.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits below Au Vignerais.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru La Maréchaude
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: La Maréchaude is a 9.3 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Vergisson, facing south. The wine is ripe and mineral.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 320 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Crays and Sur la Roche.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits below Les Crays and Sur la Roche.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Le Clos is a walled 2.7 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé, the monopole of Château-Fuissé, next to the château. The wine is rich and mineral, one of the benchmark Pouilly-Fuissés.

Les Ménétrières and Les Vignes Blanches lie nearby, on the same limestone and clay.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 265 to 290 m, gentle slope, limestone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Château-Fuissé, owned by the Vincent family, is one of the historic estates of the village of Fuissé.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos Reyssier
match: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos Reyssier
Pouilly-Fuissé Premier Cru Le Clos Reyssier
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Le Clos Reyssier is a 8.7 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Chaintré. Domaine Valette's Clos Reyssié is the reference: a rich, ripe, long white.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 230 to 270 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies below Aux Quarts.
appellations.nerd_note: Valette spells it Reyssié.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos de Monsieur Noly

Pouilly-Fuissé 1er Cru Le Clos de Monsieur Noly
Pouilly-Fuissé Premier Cru Le Clos de Monsieur Noly
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Le Clos de Monsieur Noly is a 2.7 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Chaintré. Domaine Valette makes it. The wine is rich and ripe.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 260 to 280 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the few premier crus in Burgundy named after a person with his title.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos de Solutré
match: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos de Solutré
Pouilly-Fuissé 1er Cru Le Clos de Solutré
Pouilly-Fuissé Premier Cru Le Clos de Solutré
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Le Clos de Solutré is a 4.4 ha walled Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru below the Roche de Solutré.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 290 to 330 m, steep, limestone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The Roche de Solutré gave its name to the Solutrean, a Palaeolithic culture known from the site at its foot.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Brulés
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Brûlés is a small 0.83 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé, a sun-baked site. Château-Fuissé makes it.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 305 m, steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above Les Ménétrières.
appellations.nerd_note: *Brûlé* means burnt, a common name for sun-traps.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Chevrières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Chevrières is a 11.3 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Chaintré. The wine is ripe and fine. It faces south-southwest in Chaintré, at the southern end of the appellation.
appellations.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 230 to 285 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. The gradient averages about 12%.
appellations.nerd_note: The name probably refers to goats (*chèvres*) once grazed here.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Crays
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Crays is a steep 10.8 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Vergisson, below the great limestone escarpment of the Roche de Vergisson. It was among the 22 climats promoted in 2020, the first premier crus of the Mâconnais. The wine is taut and mineral, with citrus and a stony finish, the most northern-feeling of Pouilly-Fuissé.
appellations.terroir: Steep, south-southwest-facing at 310 to 390 m, slope around 26%. Thin limestone scree and marl at the foot of the rock.
appellations.nerd_note: Vergisson's premier crus are among the highest and latest-ripening of Pouilly-Fuissé.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Ménétrières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Les Ménétrières is a 5.2 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé. Domaine Ferret's Tête de Cru Les Ménétrières is a reference: rich, ripe and mineral.

It sits between Les Reisses, Les Brûlés and Le Clos, on limestone and clay.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Ferret classified its own cuvées as Tête de Cru and Hors Classe long before the official premier crus.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Perrières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Perrières is a 5.8 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé, on stony ground once quarried. The wine is mineral and fine.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 255 to 320 m, moderately steep, stony limestone. On the map it lies below Les Vignes Blanches.
appellations.nerd_note: The same name appears on premier crus in Meursault, Puligny, Beaune, Nuits and Saint-Aubin.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Reisses
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Reisses is a 4.1 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé. The wine is ripe and fine.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 265 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies beside Les Ménétrières.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits next to Les Ménétrières.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Vignes Blanches
match: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Vignes Blanches
Pouilly-Fuissé Premier Cru Les Vignes Blanches
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Vignes Blanches is a 19.1 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé. The wine is ripe and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 270 to 350 m, steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above Les Perrières, Le Clos and Les Ménétrières.
appellations.nerd_note: The name suggests a long tradition of white grapes.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Pouilly
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Pouilly is a 19.4 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly, around the hamlet that gave half the appellation its name. The wine is ripe and fine.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 255 to 340 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above Aux Bouthières.
appellations.nerd_note: The hamlet of Pouilly is part of the commune of Solutré-Pouilly.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Sur la Roche
match: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Sur la Roche
Pouilly-Fuissé Premier Cru Sur la Roche
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Sur la Roche is a 14.8 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru high on the slope below the Roche de Vergisson. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 315 to 395 m, steep, thin limestone soils. On the map it lies above La Maréchaude.
appellations.nerd_note: The rock of Vergisson, like its neighbour at Solutré, is a landmark limestone escarpment visible across the Mâconnais.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Vers Cras
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Vers Cras is a 23.2 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru straddling Fuissé and Solutré-Pouilly. Château de Beauregard makes it. The wine is ripe and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, stony limestone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: *Cras* means stony ground.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Loché premier cru les Mûres
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Mûres is the only premier cru of Pouilly-Loché, a 7.1 ha climat recognised by the INAO at the end of 2024, with the 2024 vintage the first allowed to use the name. Pouilly-Loché is a small appellation of about 33 ha, overlapping with Pouilly-Vinzelles. The wine is a ripe, mineral Chardonnay.
appellations.terroir: Northeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, gentle slope, clay and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: The new Loché and Vinzelles premier crus are the first in Burgundy to ban all herbicides, and they require hand harvesting; Loché itself has been part of the commune of Mâcon since the 1970s.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Vinzelles premier cru Les Longeays
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Longeays is a 7.4 ha Pouilly-Vinzelles premier cru recognised by the INAO at the end of 2024, with the 2024 vintage the first to use the name.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 270 m, moderately steep, clay and limestone. On the map it lies below Pouilly-Fuissé's Aux Quarts and above Les Quarts.
appellations.nerd_note: The work to delimit Vinzelles' premier crus began in 2006 with a geological survey.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Vinzelles premier cru Les Pétaux
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Pétaux is the smallest of the three Pouilly-Vinzelles premier crus, at 2.8 ha, recognised by the INAO at the end of 2024.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, gentle slope, clay and limestone. On the map it lies beside Pouilly-Loché's les Mûres.
appellations.nerd_note: It borders Pouilly-Loché's Les Mûres.

appellations.name: Pouilly-Vinzelles premier cru Les Quarts
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Les Quarts is the largest of the three Pouilly-Vinzelles premier crus recognised by the INAO at the end of 2024, at 12.6 ha, next to Pouilly-Fuissé's Aux Quarts. The 2024 vintage was the first to use the name. Domaine La Soufrandière (the Bret Brothers) made its name here.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 220 to 270 m, moderately steep, clay and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: The rules for the new premier crus cap yields at 58 hl/ha and require at least 12% alcohol.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Champ Canet
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Champ Canet is a 4.7 ha premier cru on the slope above Les Combettes, against Meursault's Perrières. It gives a fresh, mineral Puligny with Perrières' tension. Etienne Sauzet is the largest holder.

Les Chalumaux and La Truffière lie above it. Its wines are tense and mineral, with Perrières' cut; Sauzet's and Carillon's versions show it at its best.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. The gradient is moderate, about 9%, and the stony limestone soil is shallow, which gives the wine its tension.
appellations.nerd_note: Champ Canet sits at almost the same altitude as Meursault's Perrières, and the two wines share a family resemblance.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Champ Gain
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Champ Gain is a 10.7 ha premier cru high on the slope toward Saint-Aubin. The wine is fresh and lean.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 315 to 360 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below La Garenne, above La Truffière and Les Folatières and beside Saint-Aubin's Les Murgers des dents de chien.
appellations.nerd_note: Chassagne-Montrachet also has a premier cru called Les Champs Gain.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Clavaillon
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Clavaillon is a 5.6 ha premier cru below Les Folatières. Domaine Leflaive owns most of it. The wine is supple and fruity, an accessible Puligny premier cru.

It sits on the gentle slope below Les Folatières and beside Les Pucelles and the Clos de la Mouchère, on brown limestone-clay. Leflaive's Clavaillon, from the estate's large holding, is a supple, early-drinking Puligny premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Leflaive's Clavaillon is usually its earliest-drinking premier cru.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Clos de la Garenne
match: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Clos de la Garenne
Puligny-Montrachet 1er Cru Clos de la Garenne
Puligny-Montrachet Premier Cru Clos de la Garenne
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: The Clos de la Garenne is a walled 1.9 ha premier cru within La Garenne, above Les Folatières. It is a monopole of the Duc de Magenta, made by Louis Jadot. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 280 m, moderately steep, thin stony soils.
producers: Domaine du Duc de Magenta (Louis Jadot)
appellations.nerd_note: The Duc de Magenta's family descends from Marshal MacMahon, victor of the Battle of Magenta in 1859.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Clos de la Mouchère
match: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Clos de la Mouchère
Puligny-Montrachet 1er Cru Clos de la Mouchère
Puligny-Montrachet Premier Cru Clos de la Mouchère
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: The Clos de la Mouchère is a walled 3.9 ha monopole of Domaine Henri Boillot (from the Jean Boillot holding), within Les Perrières. The wine is fine and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, gentle slope, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Clos de la Garenne and Les Folatières and beside Les Perrières and Clavaillon.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the few monopoles in Puligny.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Hameau de Blagny
match: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Hameau de Blagny
Puligny-Montrachet Premier Cru Hameau de Blagny
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: The white side of Hameau de Blagny: 4.2 ha around the hamlet. White wine from here is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru; red is Blagny premier cru.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 315 to 340 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below La Garenne, above Les Chalumaux and La Truffière and beside Meursault's Blagny.
appellations.nerd_note: Martelet de Cherisey's cellars are in the hamlet itself.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru La Garenne
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: The white side of La Garenne: 9.9 ha high above Puligny, near Blagny. White wine from here is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru, a fresh, mineral wine.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 375 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Sous le Puits and above Champ Gain, Hameau de Blagny and Saint-Aubin's Les Murgers des dents de chien.
appellations.nerd_note: The Duc de Magenta's Clos de la Garenne lies within it.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru La Truffière
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: La Truffière ('truffle ground') is a 2.5 ha premier cru high on the slope above Les Folatières, toward Blagny. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 295 to 325 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Hameau de Blagny and Champ Gain and above Les Folatières and Champ Canet.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus on the Puligny side, at over 300 m.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Le Cailleret
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Le Cailleret is the premier cru that touches Le Montrachet's northern edge and Chevalier-Montrachet, and it is widely regarded as the finest premier cru of Puligny. At 3.3 ha (close to 4 ha with the adjoining Les Demoiselles) it sits on the same mid-slope band as the grands crus. Its wine has real grand cru character: concentrated, mineral and long, with citrus, white flowers and a stony, saline finish.

Jean Chartron's walled Clos du Cailleret is a monopole within it, and Domaine de Montille makes a fine Cailleret from vines that came with the Château de Puligny-Montrachet.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 265 m. Stony limestone-clay with scree over hard limestone, close to the soils of Le Montrachet below Chevalier.
appellations.nerd_note: Its name, like Chassagne's Cailleret and Volnay's Caillerets, probably comes from stones (*cailloux*).

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Chalumaux
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Chalumaux is a 6.0 ha premier cru on the slope above Champ Canet, toward Blagny. Matrot makes it. The wine is fresh and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 285 to 325 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Meursault's Blagny, Blagny's Sous Blagny and Hameau de Blagny and beside Meursault's Sous le Dos d'Ane.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits between Puligny and the hamlet of Blagny.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Combettes
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Combettes is a 6.8 ha premier cru at the northern end of Puligny, against Meursault's Perrières and Charmes. It gives a richer, rounder Puligny than most, with some of Meursault's breadth: ripe citrus, hazelnut and a generous texture.

Champ Canet lies above and Les Referts below. Its richer, rounder style comes from its position on the Meursault border; Sauzet's and Leflaive's Combettes combine Meursault's breadth with Puligny's floral lift.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay in a slight hollow (the *combe* of the name).
appellations.nerd_note: It is the Puligny premier cru that tastes most like Meursault, and it touches both Meursault's Perrières and Charmes.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Demoiselles
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Les Demoiselles is a tiny 0.61 ha premier cru at the junction of Le Montrachet, Chevalier-Montrachet, Bâtard-Montrachet and Le Cailleret. Part of the old lieu-dit was absorbed into Chevalier-Montrachet. Guy Amiot makes a fine premier cru from it.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay like Le Cailleret.
appellations.nerd_note: Jadot and Latour's 'Chevalier-Montrachet Les Demoiselles' come from the grand cru part of the same lieu-dit.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Folatières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Folatières is the largest premier cru of Puligny, about 17.6 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 17.7 ha), on the slope above Clavaillon and Les Pucelles, rising toward Blagny. Its wine is fine and floral, with citrus and a mineral finish; the best parcels rival Les Pucelles.

Le Cailleret lies to the south and La Truffière and Champ Gain above, so the climat rises from about 250 to over 300 m. The lower part, close to Les Pucelles, gives the richest wines, the upper part the most mineral. Drouhin's and Jadot's versions are widely available and reliable.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 305 m, moderately steep. Stony limestone-clay, thin on the upper part.
appellations.nerd_note: The INAO allows several smaller lieux-dits, including Peux Bois and En la Richarde, to be sold as Folatières.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Perrières
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Perrières is a 3.5 ha premier cru on the lower slope at the northern end of Puligny, near the village. The wine is a fine, mineral Puligny.

It sits on the gentle lower slope near the village, below Les Combettes and beside Les Referts, on stony limestone. Its wines are fine and mineral, and Henri Boillot's walled Clos de la Mouchère inside it is its best-known wine.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 250 m, gentle slope, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Henri Boillot's Clos de la Mouchère lies within it.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Pucelles
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Pucelles ('the maidens') lies just north of Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet and Bâtard-Montrachet, at 6.8 ha, on the gentle lower slope. It is often ranked with Le Cailleret as Puligny's finest premier cru: its wine is the most elegant and floral of the village, with white flowers, citrus, a silky texture and a fine mineral finish. Domaine Leflaive is the largest holder, with about 3 ha.

Le Cailleret lies above it and Clavaillon beside it. Its deeper, slightly more clay-rich soil gives more breadth than Le Cailleret, but it keeps Puligny's floral, mineral finesse; Leflaive's Pucelles is one of the most famous premier cru whites in the world.
appellations.terroir: Gentle east slope at 235 to 250 m. Brown limestone-clay with more clay than Le Cailleret, over limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Leflaive's 3 ha make Les Pucelles the house's flagship premier cru, and it sits directly against Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet, which Leflaive also owns.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Referts
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Les Referts is a 5.8 ha premier cru at the northern end of Puligny, below Les Combettes and next to Meursault's Charmes. The wine is rich and round.

Its wines are rich and round, a Meursault-influenced Puligny; Sauzet's and Carillon's versions are among the best.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Its Meursault neighbour Les Charmes gives a similarly broad wine.

appellations.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Sous le Puits
match: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Sous le Puits
Puligny-Montrachet Premier Cru Sous le Puits
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted)
appellations.summary: The white side of Sous le Puits: 6.8 ha at the top of the Blagny slope. White wine from here is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru, lean and mineral.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 400 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies above Meursault's Blagny, La Garenne and Blagny's La Jeunellotte and beside Meursault's Les Ravelles.
appellations.nerd_note: *Puits* means well; the climat probably took its name from the hamlet's well.

appellations.name: Rully premier cru Agneux
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay; Pinot Noir for red
appellations.summary: Agneux is a tiny 0.57 ha Rully premier cru on the slope near the village.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 270 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Le Meix Caillet and above Molesme and Les Pierres.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in Rully.

appellations.name: Rully premier cru Champs Cloux
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay; Pinot Noir for red
appellations.summary: Champs Cloux is a 5.2 ha Rully premier cru on the slope north of the village. The white is fresh and fruity.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 265 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above La Renarde and beside La Bressande.
appellations.nerd_note: It lies next to La Bressande and La Renarde.

appellations.name: Rully premier cru Chapitre
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay; Pinot Noir for red
appellations.summary: Chapitre is a 3.8 ha Rully premier cru on the lower slope near the village, once property of a cathedral chapter. Both red and white are made.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl.
appellations.nerd_note: Several Burgundian villages have a Chapitre or Clos du Chapitre, a reminder of church ownership before 1789.

appellations.name: Rully premier cru Clos St Jacques
match: Rully premier cru Clos St Jacques
Rully Premier Cru Clos St Jacques

appellations.name: Rully premier cru Grésigny
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay; Pinot Noir for red
appellations.summary:
Grésigny is one of the best-known premier crus of Rully, the northernmost village of the Côte Chalonnaise, a 6.4 ha slope south of the village facing southeast. It is above all a white site: Chardonnay here is taut, citrus-driven and stony, a lighter, crisper cousin of a Côte de Beaune white, and Rully's whites are among the best values in Burgundy.

It sits on the slope south of the village, with Vauvry and Margotés around it, on limestone and marl. Its whites are taut and mineral, and Jacqueson's and Ninot's versions are among the best of Rully.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 310 m, moderately steep. Limestone and marl, with white marl patches that suit Chardonnay.
appellations.nerd_note: Rully was one of the cradles of Burgundian sparkling wine in the 19th century, and much of its base wine still goes into Crémant de Bourgogne.

appellations.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Derrière Chez Edouard

appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
Derrière Chez Edouard ('behind Edouard's house') is a steep 4.0 ha premier cru high above the village of Saint-Aubin. Hubert Lamy's version, including a high-density old-vine cuvée, made the name famous: a taut, mineral white of real concentration, and a fresh red.

It sits on the steep slope high above the village, beside Les Castets and Le Puits, on thin stony limestone. Its whites are taut and mineral, and Lamy's red from here is one of the best of Saint-Aubin.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 310 to 375 m, slope around 20%, thin stony limestone soil. At over 300 m and with a median gradient near 20%, it is among the coolest premier crus of Saint-Aubin.
appellations.nerd_note: Lamy planted part of it at about three times the usual Côte d'Or density, to force the roots deeper and keep yields tiny.

appellations.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru En Remilly
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary:
En Remilly is the Saint-Aubin premier cru that sits closest to the great white grands crus: its 29.5 ha slope lies just over the hill from Chevalier-Montrachet and Le Montrachet, facing southwest toward Chassagne, and a small part continues into Chassagne itself. Its white is the most complete of Saint-Aubin: citrus, white flowers and a cool, stony, saline finish with more weight than the village's higher sites.

Saint-Aubin was long the poor relation of Puligny and Chassagne, selling its wine in bulk; growers such as Hubert Lamy and Marc Colin showed from the 1990s that En Remilly could make whites of real class at a fraction of the price.
appellations.terroir: Southwest-facing at 250 to 320 m, steep in places. Thin, stony limestone soil with white marl, over Bathonian limestone; the hill behind shelters it from cold northwest winds.
appellations.nerd_note: Because it faces southwest, away from the main line of the Côte, En Remilly gets more late-afternoon sun than the east-facing grands crus just over the hill.

Marc Colin's and Hubert Lamy's versions are among the best whites of Saint-Aubin.
appellations.terroir: Steep, southwest-facing at 265 to 325 m, slope around 24%. Thin stony limestone soil with white marl. The southwest exposure catches the afternoon sun, which gives ripeness despite the altitude.
appellations.nerd_note: It is an umbrella name too: Le Bas de Gamay à l'Est may be sold as La Chatenière.

appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Combes and Le Charmois and beside Chassagne-Montrachet's Les Vergers and Les Combes au Sud.
appellations.nerd_note: The same climat appears in two villages under two spellings.

appellations.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Sous Roche Dumay
match: Saint-Aubin premier cru Sous Roche Dumay
Saint-Aubin Premier Cru Sous Roche Dumay
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Sous Roche Dumay is a steep 2.2 ha premier cru within Sur Gamay, below a limestone cliff, at the top of Saint-Aubin's slope. The white is lean and mineral.
appellations.terroir: Very steep, south-southwest-facing at 345 to 400 m, slope around 37%, thin stony soil.
appellations.nerd_note: At up to 400 m it is one of the highest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

appellations.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Sur Gamay
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Sur Gamay is a large 14.7 ha premier cru above the hamlet of Gamay, on the high slope toward Blagny. It is an umbrella for Sous Roche Dumay. The white is fresh and mineral, the red light and fruity.
appellations.terroir: Southwest-facing at 315 to 390 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soil.
appellations.nerd_note: The hamlet of Gamay, part of Saint-Aubin, is often said to have given its name to the Gamay grape.

appellations.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Sur le sentier du Clou
match: Saint-Aubin premier cru Sur le sentier du Clou
Saint-Aubin 1er Cru Sur le sentier du Clou
Saint-Aubin Premier Cru Sur le sentier du Clou
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Sur le Sentier du Clou is a 18.0 ha premier cru above the village of Saint-Aubin, facing southeast, and an umbrella for Echaille, En la Ranché, Les Travers de Marinot, Marinot and Vignes Moingeon. The white is fine and mineral, the red light.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 365 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil.
appellations.nerd_note: Wines from its five sub-climats may all be sold under the Sur le Sentier du Clou name.

appellations.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Vignes Moingeon
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Vignes Moingeon is a 4.8 ha premier cru within Sur le Sentier du Clou, just above the village.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 280 to 335 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Sur le sentier du Clou and En la Ranché and above Es Champs and Les Frionnes.
appellations.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Sur le Sentier du Clou.

appellations.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Village
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
appellations.summary: Village is a 2.8 ha premier cru at the edge of the village of Saint-Aubin. The wine is a fresh white or a light red.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 310 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Sur le sentier du Clou and Echaille, above Les Frionnes and beside Les Perrières.
appellations.nerd_note: Several Côte d'Or villages have a premier cru named for the village itself.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Beauregard
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Beauregard ('fine view') is a 18.1 ha premier cru on the steep slope above the village of Santenay. The red is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: Steep, south-southeast-facing at 250 to 325 m, slope around 18%, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above Les Gravières, La Comme and Clos des Mouches and beside Clos Faubard.
appellations.nerd_note: Its upper reaches look over the Dheune valley toward the Côte Chalonnaise.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Beaurepaire
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Beaurepaire is a steep 14.7 ha premier cru above Santenay-le-Haut, facing south. It makes both a fresh red and a mineral white.
appellations.terroir: Steep, south-facing at 250 to 350 m, slope around 24%, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above La Maladière.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus in Santenay.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Clos Faubard
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: The Clos Faubard is a 4.0 ha premier cru above the village of Santenay. The red is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above Clos des Mouches and beside Beauregard.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits between Beauregard and the Clos des Mouches.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Clos Rousseau
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: The Clos Rousseau is a 15.8 ha premier cru at the southern end of Santenay, against the Maranges. The red is supple and fruity.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 300 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Grand Clos Rousseau, Maranges's La Fussière and Maranges's Les Clos Roussots and beside Maranges's Clos de la Boutière.
appellations.nerd_note: It continues into the Maranges as Les Clos Roussots.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Clos de Tavannes
match: Santenay premier cru Clos de Tavannes
Santenay Premier Cru Clos de Tavannes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: The Clos de Tavannes is a 5.3 ha premier cru within Les Gravières, against Chassagne's Morgeot. Its red is one of the most structured of Santenay. Pousse d'Or makes a well-known version.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, gravelly limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Les Gravières and beside Chassagne-Montrachet's Morgeot, Chassagne-Montrachet's Les Brussonnes and Chassagne-Montrachet's La Grande Borne.
appellations.nerd_note: The INAO lists it both alone and as Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Clos des Mouches
match: Santenay premier cru Clos des Mouches
Santenay Premier Cru Clos des Mouches
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Santenay's Clos des Mouches is a 2.8 ha premier cru above the village, not to be confused with Beaune's famous namesake. The red is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 255 to 275 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil.
appellations.nerd_note: Beaune's Clos des Mouches is about 15 km to the north; the shared name is a coincidence of old field names.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Grand Clos Rousseau
match: Santenay premier cru Grand Clos Rousseau
Santenay Premier Cru Grand Clos Rousseau
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: The Grand Clos Rousseau is a 8.0 ha premier cru above the Clos Rousseau, at the southern end of Santenay. The red is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 335 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Maranges's La Fussière and above Clos Rousseau.
appellations.nerd_note: It borders the Maranges' La Fussière.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru La Comme
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: La Comme is a large 22.0 ha premier cru above Les Gravières, on the slope toward Chassagne. Its red is firm and dark-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 305 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Beauregard and Chassagne-Montrachet's Bois de Chassagne and above Les Gravières and Chassagne-Montrachet's Morgeot.
appellations.nerd_note: It borders Chassagne's Bois de Chassagne and Clos Pitois to the north.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru La Maladière
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: La Maladière is a 13.6 ha premier cru above Santenay, toward Dezize. The name refers to a medieval leper hospital (*maladrerie*). The red is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 305 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Many Burgundy villages have a Maladière, usually on the edge of the old settlement, where the sick were kept apart.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Les Gravières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Gravières is the best-known premier cru of Santenay, a 29.5 ha slope just south of Chassagne's Morgeot, at the northern end of the commune. The name comes from its gravelly soil. The red is the finest of Santenay: perfumed, red-fruited and firm, with more finesse than the village's other reds; a little white is also made.

It sits on the gentle slope at the northern end of Santenay, against Chassagne's Morgeot, with La Comme above and Passetemps below. Its gravelly soil gives the finest red of Santenay, and Vincent's, Girardin's and Belland's versions are references.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 220 to 260 m, gentle slope. Gravelly limestone-clay over limestone, free-draining.
appellations.nerd_note: It is an umbrella for the Clos de Tavannes, which also has its own premier cru name.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes
match: Santenay premier cru Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes
Santenay 1er Cru Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes
Santenay Premier Cru Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes is the double name under which the Clos de Tavannes (5.3 ha) may be sold, within Les Gravières.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, gravelly limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Les Gravières and beside Chassagne-Montrachet's Morgeot, Chassagne-Montrachet's Les Brussonnes and Chassagne-Montrachet's La Grande Borne.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of a handful of premier crus that may carry two climat names on the label.

appellations.name: Santenay premier cru Passetemps
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Passetemps ('pastime') is a 11.7 ha premier cru below the village of Santenay. The red is supple and fruity.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 225 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Clos des Mouches and beside Les Gravières.
appellations.nerd_note: Santenay was also a spa town: its lithium-rich spring drew visitors in the 19th century, and the village still has a casino.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Clous
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Aux Clous is a 10.0 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, next to Aux Serpentières. The wine is a supple, red-fruited Savigny.
appellations.terroir: Gentle south slope at 255 to 285 m, on brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Aux Guettes and beside Aux Serpentières.
appellations.nerd_note: It lies at the foot of Aux Guettes, on the warm, south-facing side of the valley.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Fourneaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Aux Fourneaux is a 6.2 ha premier cru at the foot of Savigny's north slope, near the Pernand boundary. Simon Bize and Chandon de Briailles make it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Fourneaux (ovens or kilns) is a recurring climat name; there are also premier crus called Les Fourneaux in Chablis and Mercurey.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Gravains
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Aux Gravains is a 6.3 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, named for its gravel. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Gentle south slope at 255 to 265 m, on gravelly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Petits Godeaux and beside Aux Serpentières and Les Lavières.
appellations.nerd_note: Gravel washed down from the slopes above gives the soils here good drainage.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Guettes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Aux Guettes is a large, steep 14.5 ha premier cru high on Savigny's north slope, above Aux Serpentières. The wine is firm, structured and long-lived, the most tannic of the village.

Aux Serpentières and Aux Clous lie below it, and its almost due-south exposure on thin, stony limestone gives both ripeness and tannin. Bize's and Pavelot's Guettes are among the longest-lived reds of the village.
appellations.terroir: Steep, south-facing at 275 to 330 m, slope around 21%. Thin, stony limestone soils. At 275 to 330 m, it is the highest premier cru on the Pernand side of Savigny.
appellations.nerd_note: Its steep slope and south exposure make it one of the warmest sites in Savigny.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Serpentières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Aux Serpentières is a 12.7 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, below Aux Guettes. The wine is supple and red-fruited, with a gentle tannin.
appellations.terroir: Gentle south slope at 255 to 280 m, on brown limestone-clay with gravel.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits on the warm, south-facing side of the Savigny valley, where the Rhoin stream leaves the hills.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Basses Vergelesses
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Basses Vergelesses is a small 1.7 ha premier cru on the lower part of the Vergelesses slope, at the Pernand boundary. The wine is a supple, red-fruited Savigny.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Bataillère, above Les Lavières and Pernand-Vergelesses's Vergelesses and beside Pernand-Vergelesses's Ile des Vergelesses.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits between Pernand's Ile des Vergelesses and Savigny's Les Lavières.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Bataillère
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: La Bataillère is a 1.8 ha premier cru on the Vergelesses slope. Domaine Albert Morot makes it as a monopole, labelled 'La Bataillère aux Vergelesses'. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 275 to 295 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Morot's labels attach the better-known Vergelesses name to Bataillère, a common Burgundian practice for small climats.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Champ Chevrey
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Champ Chevrey is a 1.4 ha premier cru at the foot of Savigny's north slope, a monopole of Domaine Tollot-Beaut. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Lavières and beside Aux Fourneaux.
appellations.nerd_note: Tollot-Beaut's Champ Chevrey is one of the few monopoles in Savigny.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru La Dominode
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
La Dominode is the best-known premier cru on Savigny's south slope, the one that faces Beaune. At 7.9 ha it lies on the gentle lower slope, and it is famous for its old vines: Bruno Clair's Dominode comes from vines planted in 1902. The wine is deeper and more structured than the north-side premier crus, with dark fruit and earth.

It sits on the gentle lower part of the Beaune-facing slope, with Les Jarrons and Les Hauts Jarrons above and Les Narbantons and Les Marconnets alongside. Its old vines and deeper, more clay-rich soil give Savigny's darkest, most structured reds, and Pavelot and Camus-Bruchon make classic versions alongside Bruno Clair's centenarian vines.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay with more clay than the north slope.
appellations.nerd_note: Its northeast-facing slope is unusual for a premier cru, but the old vines more than make up for the cooler exposure.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Charnières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Charnières is a 2.0 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, near Les Lavières. The wine is a supple Savigny premier cru.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 280 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Talmettes and above Les Lavières.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the smaller premier crus of the Vergelesses side.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Hauts Jarrons
match: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Hauts Jarrons
Savigny-lès-Beaune Premier Cru Les Hauts Jarrons
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Hauts Jarrons is a 4.4 ha premier cru above Les Jarrons, on Savigny's south slope. The wine is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above La Dominode, Les Hauts Marconnets and Les Rouvrettes and beside Redrescul.
appellations.nerd_note: Its northeast exposure makes it one of the cooler premier crus in the village.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Hauts Marconnets
match: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Hauts Marconnets
Savigny-lès-Beaune Premier Cru Les Hauts Marconnets
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Hauts Marconnets is a 5.4 ha premier cru above Les Marconnets, on Savigny's south slope. The wine is firm and fresh.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 280 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Hauts Jarrons and above Les Marconnets, Les Peuillets and La Dominode.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus on the Beaune side of Savigny.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Jarrons
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Jarrons is a 1.5 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, above La Dominode. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Savigny.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Hauts Jarrons, above Les Narbantons and beside La Dominode and Les Rouvrettes.
appellations.nerd_note: Les Jarrons and Les Hauts Jarrons together sit just above La Dominode on the Beaune-facing slope.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Lavières
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Lavières is Savigny's largest premier cru on the north side of the village, at 17.9 ha, on the gentle south-facing slope below the Vergelesses. The name comes from *laves*, the flat limestone slabs that cover the ground. The wine is perfumed, red-fruited and silky, the most charming of Savigny's premier crus.

Les Talmettes and the Vergelesses lie above it, Aux Gravains and Aux Fourneaux alongside. The flat stones in its soil warm quickly, which helps explain its ripe, charming wines; Chandon de Briailles and Tollot-Beaut make classic versions.
appellations.terroir: Gentle south slope at 255 to 275 m. Stony limestone soils covered in flat slabs of rock.
appellations.nerd_note: *Laves*, the flat limestone slabs that give Lavières its name, were the traditional roofing stone of the Côte's dry-stone vineyard huts.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Marconnets
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Marconnets is a 3.0 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, at the Beaune boundary. It continues Beaune's Les Marconnets. Simon Bize makes it. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The climat straddles the commune boundary, so Marconnets exists as both a Savigny and a Beaune premier cru.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Narbantons
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Narbantons is a 9.6 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, next to La Dominode. Leroy, Pavelot and Écard make it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at about 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Dominode, Les Jarrons and Les Rouvrettes and beside Les Peuillets.
appellations.nerd_note: Leroy bottles it, a sign of the climat's standing among Savigny's growers.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Peuillets
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Peuillets is a large 16.0 ha premier cru on the lowest part of Savigny's south slope, toward Beaune. The wine is a fruity, early-drinking Savigny.
appellations.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at 240 to 250 m, on deep brown clay with gravel.
appellations.nerd_note: At around 240 m it is one of the lowest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Rouvrettes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Rouvrettes is a 2.7 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, below Redrescul. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Savigny.
appellations.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 255 to 270 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Redrescul and Les Hauts Jarrons, above Les Narbantons and beside Les Jarrons.
appellations.nerd_note: The name probably refers to small oaks (*rouvres*), a reminder that woodland once came further down the slope.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Talmettes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Les Talmettes is a 3.1 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, between Les Vergelesses and Les Lavières. Simon Bize makes it. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 275 to 320 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Vergelesses and above Les Lavières and Les Charnières.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits midway up the slope between the Vergelesses and Lavières.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Vergelesses
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary:
Les Vergelesses (often labelled Aux Vergelesses) is Savigny's most celebrated premier cru, a 15.2 ha slope on the north side of the village that continues the hill of Pernand's Ile des Vergelesses. Its red is the finest and longest-lived of the village: red cherry, raspberry and spice, with a firm but fine tannin and a mineral, slightly iron-tinged finish.

Simon Bize, Chandon de Briailles and Pavelot make the reference wines, and a little white is also made.

Les Basses Vergelesses, La Bataillère and Les Lavières lie below it, and it touches Pernand's Ile des Vergelesses and Creux de la Net. Its altitude and iron-rich soils give the most structured red of the village; Simon Bize's version, from an estate that has done much to raise Savigny's reputation, is the reference.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 335 m, moderately steep. Iron-rich brown limestone with marl and ferruginous oolite, at the top of Savigny's north slope.
appellations.nerd_note: The Vergelesses run across the boundary into Pernand-Vergelesses, so the same name appears on two villages' premier crus.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Petits Godeaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
appellations.summary: Petits Godeaux is a tiny 0.69 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, near Les Lavières. The wine is usually blended into a Savigny premier cru.
appellations.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Aux Serpentières, Les Lavières and Aux Gravains.
appellations.nerd_note: At under a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus in Savigny.

appellations.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Redrescul

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Clos des 60 ouvrées

appellations.summary:
The Clos des 60 Ouvrées is a 2.4 ha walled monopole of Domaine de la Pousse d'Or within Les Caillerets. An *ouvrée* is the area one man could work in a day, about 4.3 ares, so 60 ouvrées is roughly 2.6 ha. The wine is the purest Caillerets: perfumed, red-fruited and silky, with a mineral finish.

The clos sits on the southern part of Les Caillerets, toward Meursault's Les Caillerets and below the Clos des Chênes, on stony limestone-clay. It is the wine that made the Pousse d'Or's reputation under Gérard Potel from the 1960s, and it remains one of the most complete Volnays: fine-grained, perfumed and long.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The *ouvrée*, the old Burgundian unit of vineyard area, is still used in conversation by growers today.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Clos des Chênes
match: Volnay premier cru Clos des Chênes
Volnay Premier Cru Clos des Chênes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Chênes ('oaks') is a large 15.4 ha premier cru high on the slope south of the village, toward Monthélie. It is one of Volnay's most structured premier crus, with red and black fruit and a firm, mineral finish. Michel Lafarge's Clos des Chênes is a benchmark.

It is the largest of Volnay's top premier crus, high on the slope above Taille Pieds and Les Caillerets, running toward Monthélie's Les Champs Fulliots and Sur la Velle. The altitude and stony soil give a firmer, more structured Volnay than the village's lower climats, and Lafarge's and Lafon's versions age for decades.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 320 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils with scree.
appellations.nerd_note: Its upper reaches look over the Monthélie side valley.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Clos des Ducs

appellations.summary:
The Clos des Ducs is a walled 2.4 ha monopole of Domaine Marquis d'Angerville, just above the village, near the site of the castle of the Dukes of Burgundy. It is regarded as the most perfumed and refined of Volnay's great premier crus: red cherry, rose, spice and a silky, mineral structure that ages for decades.

The d'Angerville family were among the pioneers of domaine bottling in the 1930s, alongside Henri Gouges and Armand Rousseau, and Guillaume d'Angerville, son of the late Marquis Jacques, has run the estate since 2003.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 325 m, moderately steep. Thin white limestone soils with scree over hard Bathonian limestone; very little clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The estate propagates its own Pinot Noir selection, known as 'Pinot d'Angerville', which it has kept for generations.

Frémiets is a 5.9 ha premier cru on the slope north of the village, toward Pommard. D'Angerville and Voillot make it. The wine is fine and red-fruited.

It sits on the slope just north of the village, below Pitures Dessus and above Les Brouillards and Les Angles, touching Pommard's Les Jarolières and Les Fremiers. Its wines have more structure than most Volnays, a Pommard influence, and d'Angerville's Fremiet is a good example.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: It continues Pommard's Les Fremiers across the commune line.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Les Angles
