appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Frémiets, Clos de la Barre and Frémiets Clos de la Rougeotte and above Les Brouillards.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits between Les Brouillards and the village.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Les Brouillards
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Brouillards ('the mists') is a 5.6 ha premier cru on the lower slope north of the village, toward Pommard. The wine is supple and perfumed.

Les Mitans and Les Angles lie alongside, and it touches Pommard's Les Combes Dessus and Les Fremiers. De Montille's version is a delicate, early-drinking classic.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 4%, and the soil deeper than in the upper climats, giving a softer wine.
appellations.nerd_note: The name means 'the mists'; it is one of the few Volnay premier crus on the Pommard side of the village.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Les Caillerets
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Caillerets is usually ranked the finest premier cru of Volnay, a 12.1 ha climat on the mid-slope south of the village, toward Meursault. The name comes from its stones (*cailloux*). Its wine combines Volnay's perfume with real depth: red cherry, raspberry, violet and spice, a silky texture and a long, mineral finish, more structured than most Volnay.

The Clos des 60 Ouvrées, Pousse d'Or's monopole, lies within it and has its own premier cru name. Other leading holders include the Marquis d'Angerville, Bouchard Père et Fils (its 'Ancienne Cuvée Carnot'), Michel Lafarge and Joseph Voillot.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 290 m. Stony red-brown limestone-clay over hard limestone, with scree on the upper part and more clay below.
appellations.nerd_note: Bouchard's 'Caillerets Ancienne Cuvée Carnot' is named after the Carnot family, the parcel's former owners.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Les Lurets
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Les Lurets is a 2.1 ha premier cru on the lower slope south of the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Caillerets and En Chevret and beside Robardelle and Le Ronceret.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus in Volnay.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Les Mitans
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Mitans ('the middle') is a 8.6 ha premier cru on the lower slope below the village. De Montille and d'Angerville make it. The wine is fine and red-fruited.

It sits on the gentle slope below the village, between Les Brouillards and Carelle sous la Chapelle, on brown limestone-clay. Its wines are fine and red-fruited, with a little more depth than Les Brouillards, and d'Angerville's and de Montille's versions are references.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: It lies midway between the village and the Route nationale.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Pitures Dessus
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Pitures Dessus is a 6.7 ha premier cru high on the slope above the village, toward Pommard. The wine is fresh and fine.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 340 m, steep, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Pommard's Les Chanlins-Bas, Frémiets and Frémiets Clos de la Rougeotte and beside Clos des Ducs.
appellations.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus in Volnay.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Robardelle
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Robardelle is a 2.9 ha premier cru on the lower slope south of the village, toward Meursault. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Santenots, En Chevret and Les Caillerets and beside Les Lurets.
appellations.nerd_note: It sits just above the Santenots.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Santenots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Santenots is the strangest premier cru in Volnay: it lies entirely in the commune of Meursault, on the slope south of Volnay's Caillerets, but its red wine is sold as Volnay premier cru (Volnay-Santenots), while white from the same vines is Meursault premier cru. The umbrella covers 29.0 ha, including Les Santenots du Milieu, Les Santenots Blancs and Les Plures.

The wine is Volnay with a Meursault accent: fuller, darker and earthier than the Volnays of the village, with black cherry and spice. Comtes Lafon's Santenots-du-Milieu and Jacques Prieur's Clos des Santenots are the benchmarks.
appellations.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 275 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay with more marl and clay than Volnay's own premier crus.
appellations.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Jehan de Massol and Gauvain are Volnay-Santenots.

appellations.name: Volnay premier cru Taille Pieds
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Taille Pieds (Taillepieds) is a 7.2 ha premier cru on the steep slope just south of the village. The name is usually explained as 'cut feet', from the effort of working the steep slope. Its wines are among the most refined in Volnay: perfumed, red-fruited, silky and long, with a mineral finish. De Montille's Taillepieds is a reference.

The Clos des Chênes lies above and Champans below, with the Clos de l'Audignac and the Clos du Verseuil toward the village. Its thin white limestone gives the most aerial Volnay of all: rose, red cherry and a fine, mineral spine. The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Blondeau and Général Muteau both include Taille Pieds.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 270 to 320 m, slope around 14%. Thin white limestone soils with scree.
appellations.nerd_note: Taille Pieds, Clos des Ducs and Caillerets are usually named as Volnay's top three premier crus.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Au-dessus des Malconsorts
match: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Au-dessus des Malconsorts
Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Au-dessus des Malconsorts
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Au-dessus des Malconsorts ('above Malconsorts') is a steep 1.1 ha strip at the top of the slope, between Malconsorts and La Tâche's upper reaches. The soil is thin and the wine lighter and fresher than Malconsorts, with red fruit and a stony finish.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 280 to 310 m, slope around 23%. Thin stony soil over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Its lower edge touches La Tâche, the most consistent of the Vosne grands crus.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Aux Brulées
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Aux Brulées sits above Richebourg, at 4.6 ha, between Les Beaux Monts and Cros Parantoux, and in the best hands it is one of Vosne's three or four finest premier crus. The name ('the burnt ones') points to its warm, sun-catching position on the upper slope. The wine is rich and spicy, with dark cherry, plum and a velvety, ample texture; it is more generous than Cros Parantoux next door and has some of Richebourg's opulence.

Méo-Camuzet, Grivot, Leroy and Bruno Clavelier all make fine versions, and Méo's was made by Henri Jayer, who farmed the estate's vines as a sharecropper until 1988.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep. Thin brown limestone soil over hard rock at the top of the slope.
appellations.nerd_note: The Brulées, Cros Parantoux and the upper Richebourg sit on the same band of thin soil over hard limestone, but Brulées faces more to the southeast and ripens earlier.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Aux Malconsorts
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Aux Malconsorts lies immediately south of La Tâche, at the southern end of Vosne, on the border with Nuits-Saint-Georges. The part next to La Tâche is regarded as grand cru in all but name, and its wines have La Tâche's spice and depth: dark cherry, Asian spices and a velvet tannin.

The INAO delimitation gives 5.9 ha. Domaine de Montille makes a 'Cuvée Christiane' from the oldest vines next to La Tâche, part of the old Thomas-Moillard holding that de Montille and Dujac bought in 2005. Sylvain Cathiard's Malconsorts is a reference, and Lamarche and Hudelot-Noëllat also make it.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 285 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay with plenty of stones, over Bajocian and Bathonian limestone; the upper part is close in soil to La Tâche.
appellations.nerd_note: The name is usually translated as 'bad companions', though no one knows who the troublemakers were.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Aux Raignots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Aux Raignots (also Reignots) is a steep 1.6 ha premier cru above La Romanée and La Grande Rue. Comte Liger-Belair's version is a benchmark. The wine is fine, mineral and perfumed, a higher, leaner cousin of the grands crus below.

The climat climbs steeply above La Romanée, the Liger-Belair grand cru, and its upper part reaches the woods. Comte Liger-Belair's Reignots, from the family's historic holding, is usually the most refined of its premier crus, with the perfume of the grands crus below in a cooler, more mineral frame.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 275 to 340 m, slope around 22%. Thin soil and rubble over hard limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Its lower edge touches three grands crus: La Romanée, La Grande Rue and Richebourg.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Clos des Réas
match: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Clos des Réas
Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Clos des Réas
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
The Clos des Réas is a walled 2.1 ha premier cru on the southern edge of Vosne's village, a monopole of Domaine Michel Gros. The wine is supple and perfumed, with red fruit and silky tannin.

The clos sits on flat ground at the southern edge of the village, next to Les Chaumes, and Michel Gros' version is the archetype of a charming, early-drinking Vosne premier cru: red cherry, spice and silk. It is one of the few monopoles in Vosne outside the grands crus.
appellations.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at about 245 m, on deep brown limestone-clay. The almost flat ground, about 3% gradient, and deep soil explain the wine's soft, early charm.
appellations.nerd_note: The Gros family has owned the clos since 1860.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Cros Parantoux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Cros Parantoux is the premier cru that Henri Jayer made into a legend. It is a little hollow (*cros*) of about 1 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 1.0 ha) tucked above Richebourg, cooler and higher than the grands crus below it. After phylloxera it lay abandoned and during the Second World War it grew Jerusalem artichokes; from 1951 Jayer cleared and replanted it, famously using dynamite to break the rock.

Jayer's Cros Parantoux from the 1970s to the mid-1990s are among the most expensive red wines ever sold at auction. Today the vineyard is split between Emmanuel Rouget, Jayer's nephew and successor (about 0.7 ha), and Domaine Méo-Camuzet (about 0.3 ha), whose parcel Jayer farmed as a sharecropper until 1988.

The wine is less exuberant than Richebourg and more mineral: dark cherry, violet, spice and a cool, precise structure that needs ten years or more.
appellations.terroir: A small fold in the slope at 280 to 300 m, opening to the east and northeast, so it gets less afternoon sun than Richebourg. Thin soil and rubble over hard limestone at the top of the slope; the cooler exposure gives later ripening and higher acidity.
appellations.nerd_note: Rouget still makes the wine in Jayer's cellar style, and both his and Méo-Camuzet's bottles are among the most tightly allocated in Burgundy.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru En Orveaux
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
En Orveaux is a 1.9 ha premier cru in Flagey-Echezeaux, sold as Vosne-Romanée, on the slope near the Combe d'Orveau above Echezeaux. Cathiard's En Orveaux is the best-known. The wine is cool and fine-boned.

It sits on the slope above the Echezeaux grand cru, on cool ground near the Combe d'Orveau, and its wines are among the most delicate and perfumed of the Vosne premier crus. Sylvain Cathiard's En Orveaux is the classic: red fruit, flowers and fine, silky tannin.
appellations.terroir: Northeast-facing at 280 to 310 m, moderately steep, on thin brown limestone soils. The northeast-facing slope is cool, which slows ripening and preserves the wine's delicate perfume.
appellations.nerd_note: Part of the lieu-dit En Orveaux is grand cru Echezeaux; only the upper part is premier cru.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru La Croix Rameau
match: Vosne-Romanée premier cru La Croix Rameau
Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru La Croix Rameau
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
La Croix Rameau is the smallest premier cru of Vosne at 0.60 ha, a pocket against the northern edge of Romanée-Saint-Vivant. Its soils and position are hard to distinguish from the grand cru, and growers have long argued it should be part of it. Lamarche, Cacheux and Coudray-Bizot share it.

Its soils are deep brown limestone-clay, like those of the lower Romanée-Saint-Vivant, and its wines show the same floral, spicy character in a slightly softer form. Lamarche's version, from a domaine whose own grand cru La Grande Rue was promoted in 1992, is the best-known.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay like Romanée-Saint-Vivant.
appellations.nerd_note: At about 0.6 ha it is smaller than several single-family holdings in the neighbouring grand cru.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Beaux Monts
match: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Beaux Monts
Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Les Beaux Monts
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Beaux Monts lies largely in the commune of Flagey-Echezeaux but is sold as Vosne-Romanée premier cru. At 12.0 ha it climbs the slope above Echezeaux and Les Suchots, and is split into Beaux Monts Bas and Hauts. The wines are fine, cool and perfumed, with more mineral tension than Les Suchots.

Leroy, Jean Grivot and Louis Jadot are major holders.

The INAO figures show that about 7.6 of its 12 ha lie in Flagey-Echezeaux and the rest in Vosne. It sits above the Suchots and next to the upper Echezeaux, on thinner, cooler ground than the lower premier crus, which is why it was a late-ripening site in the 20th century and has become one of the most sought-after Vosne premier crus in the warmer 21st.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 325 m, moderately steep. Thin brown limestone soils with stony rubble, over hard Bathonian limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Its lower section, Les Beaux Monts Bas, touches Echezeaux, while the top reaches the woods at more than 320 m.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Chaumes
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Chaumes sits below La Tâche and Malconsorts on the flatter lower slope, at 6.9 ha. The wine is fruity, supple and early-drinking, a generous Vosne premier cru.

It lies on the flat lower ground east of Malconsorts and La Tâche, next to the Clos des Réas and running south to Nuits' Aux Boudots. Deep soil and gentle slope make it the most approachable of Vosne's premier crus, ready after five years, but the top versions from Méo-Camuzet and Arnoux-Lachaux have real depth.
appellations.terroir: Gentle east slope at 245 to 255 m, on deep brown limestone-clay. At around 245 to 255 m, it is one of the lowest premier crus of Vosne.
appellations.nerd_note: *Chaumes* means fallow or stubble ground, a common name for low-lying fields.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Gaudichots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Les Gaudichots is a tiny remnant: most of the original lieu-dit was absorbed into La Tâche in the 1930s, after the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti bought the Liger-Belair La Tâche and the Gaudichots parcels were allowed to take the grand cru name. The 0.80 ha that remain premier cru lie beside and above La Tâche.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 310 m, moderately steep, on thin stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Forey is the main producer of Les Gaudichots premier cru today.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Petits Monts
match: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Petis Monts
Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Les Petis Monts
Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Petits Monts
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Petits Monts (written 'Les Petis Monts' in the INAO register) is a steep 3.7 ha premier cru at the top of the slope above Richebourg and La Romanée. The wine is fine and cool, with red fruit and a mineral finish.

It sits on the steep upper slope above Richebourg and La Romanée, between Aux Raignots and Cros Parantoux, on thin soil over hard limestone. The register's 'Les Petis Monts' is a spelling quirk; labels say Les Petits Monts. Drouhin's version is the most widely available and shows the climat's cool, mineral elegance.
appellations.terroir: Steep, east-northeast-facing at 280 to 340 m. Thin, rocky soil on hard limestone. The northeast exposure and thin soil make it one of the coolest premier crus of Vosne.
appellations.nerd_note: Its neighbour Cros Parantoux sits just below its northern end.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Rouges
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Les Rouges is a high 2.6 ha premier cru in Flagey-Echezeaux, sold as Vosne-Romanée, above Echezeaux and Les Beaux Monts. The name comes from its reddish soil. The wine is fresh and cool, with red fruit.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 295 to 335 m, steep, on thin reddish limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Like the Beaux Monts and En Orveaux, it lies in Flagey but takes the Vosne name.

appellations.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Suchots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir
appellations.summary:
Les Suchots is the largest premier cru in Vosne, at about 13 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 13.1 ha), on the gentle slope between Richebourg and Romanée-Saint-Vivant to the south and Echezeaux to the north. It is ranked just behind Cros Parantoux and Malconsorts, and its best wines rival Echezeaux.

The wine is perfumed and generous, with red and black cherry, spice and Vosne's silky, layered texture; it is slightly softer than Malconsorts. Comte Liger-Belair, Hudelot-Noëllat, Arnoux-Lachaux and Grivot all make fine versions.

Because it is large and lies between three grands crus, Les Suchots varies: the upper part, below the Beaux Monts and Aux Brulées and next to Richebourg, gives the most intense wines, while the lower part near La Croix Rameau and Romanée-Saint-Vivant is softer and more fragrant. Many growers argue that the best parcels deserve grand cru status as much as some of Echezeaux.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay, deeper than in the grands crus above, over Bajocian limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Les Suchots touches three grands crus: Richebourg, Romanée-Saint-Vivant and Echezeaux.

appellations.name: Vougeot premier cru Clos de la Perrière
match: Vougeot premier cru Clos de la Perrière
Vougeot 1er Cru Clos de la Perrière
Vougeot Premier Cru Clos de la Perrière
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
The Clos de la Perrière is a walled 2.1 ha premier cru just outside the north wall of Clos de Vougeot, next to Les Amoureuses and Musigny. It was an old quarry, hence the name, and it is a monopole of Domaine Bertagna. The wine is supple and perfumed, with Chambolle's grace and Vougeot's warmth.

The clos sits on the steeper ground just outside the northwest corner of the Clos de Vougeot walls, between Musigny and Les Amoureuses above and the Petits Vougeots below. That thin, stony upper-slope soil explains its finesse, which many find closer to Chambolle than to the broader wines of the lower Clos de Vougeot.
appellations.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, moderately steep. Thin stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Clos de Vougeot's grand cru vines begin on the other side of the wall, one of the sharpest classification boundaries on the Côte.

appellations.name: Vougeot premier cru Le Clos Blanc
match: Vougeot premier cru Le Clos Blanc
Vougeot Premier Cru Le Clos Blanc
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay; Pinot Noir for red
appellations.summary:
Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot is one of the few walled white-wine vineyards on the Côte de Nuits. It is said to have been planted in 1110 by the Cistercian monks of Cîteaux, just outside the walls of their Clos de Vougeot. At 2.3 ha it is today a monopole of Domaine de la Vougeraie, which took it over from L'Héritier-Guyot.

The wine is mainly Chardonnay, and it is firmer and more mineral than most Côte de Beaune whites: lemon, white flowers and a salty, stony finish.
appellations.terroir: Gentle east-northeast slope at 245 to 255 m, just north of the Clos de Vougeot walls. White marl and limestone soils, paler and more calcareous than the brown soils of the clos.
appellations.nerd_note: The clos takes its name from its white grapes and pale soil, not from any colour of wine.

appellations.name: Vougeot premier cru Les Crâs
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary: Les Crâs is a 3.8 ha premier cru at the northeastern corner of Vougeot, just outside the walls of the Clos and next to the Route des Grands Crus. The wine is a supple, perfumed Vougeot premier cru, mostly red.
appellations.terroir: Almost flat, northeast exposure at about 245 m, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: *Cras* means stony ground, and the same name turns up in Chambolle, Nuits and Meursault.

appellations.name: Vougeot premier cru Les Petits Vougeots
match: Vougeot premier cru Les Petits Vougeots
Vougeot Premier Cru Les Petits Vougeots
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
appellations.summary:
Les Petits Vougeots is the largest of Vougeot's four premier crus, at 5.2 ha, just outside the north wall of Clos de Vougeot below Les Amoureuses. It gives a supple, perfumed red with Chambolle's red fruit and silk.

It sits directly below Les Amoureuses and outside the northern wall of the Clos de Vougeot, on deeper, more clay-rich soil than its Chambolle neighbour. The result is a wine with Chambolle's red fruit and perfume and a little more weight, often a good-value alternative to the grand cru next door.
appellations.terroir: East-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, on brown limestone-clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Vougeot is one of the smallest communes in Burgundy, and almost all of its vineyard is either Clos de Vougeot grand cru or these four premier crus.
